definition_zh: 相交；交叉；贯穿；与……交叠；相互联系；横穿
definition_en: to cut across each other or pass through something, so that two lines, paths, areas or ideas meet at a point or share a part
core_image: 两条线在纸面上交叉，留下一个小小的交点
scene: 在城市中心的十字路口，两条主干道在这里相遇。Two main roads intersect at the busy junction near the station.
sceneCN: 这里 intersect 是「相交、交叉」（第 1 个义项：线条或道路彼此交叉于一点）；句意为两条主干道在车站附近繁忙的十字路口相交。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「交叉点、十字路口」
现在分词作形容词，义为「相交的、交叉的」
由 intersection 加 -al 构成，义为「交叉性的；多重身份交叉的」
过去分词作形容词，义为「被横穿的、被切开的」

senses.title: Lines or paths crossing at a point
senses.definition: to cut across each other so that lines, roads or paths meet at a point
senses.definitionCN: 彼此交叉，使线条、道路或路径在某一点相遇
senses.example: The two walkways intersect near the fountain.
senses.exampleCN: 两条步道在喷泉附近相交。
senses.why: Latin intersecare joins inter, among, with secare, to cut, so the core picture is two lines cutting into each other and leaving a point where they touch.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intersecare 由 inter（在……之间）与 secare（切、割）合成，核心画面是两条线互相切入，留下一个相接的点。

senses.title: To cut through or divide a whole
senses.definition: to pass across or through something, especially so as to cut or divide it
senses.definitionCN: 经过或穿过某物，尤指把它切开或分开
senses.example: A narrow channel intersects the northern half of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 一条狭窄的水道横穿田野的北半部。
senses.why: The original verb secare means to cut, so the transitive use keeps the image of a line passing through a surface and splitting it into parts.
senses.whyCN: 原动词 secare 本义是「切」，所以及物用法保留了「一条线穿过面并把面分成几块」的画面。

senses.title: Areas that share a part
senses.definition: to meet or overlap in such a way that two areas or sets share some points or members
senses.definitionCN: 以两点范围或集合共享部分点或成员的方式相遇或重合
senses.example: In the diagram two large circles intersect and share a small region.
senses.exampleCN: 图中两个大圆相交，共享一小块区域。
senses.why: Two outlines that cut across each other enclose one shared piece, so the cutting image grows into the idea of overlapping territory.
senses.whyCN: 两个轮廓互相穿过时会围出一块共同的部分，于是「切」的画面延伸到「领域交叠」的含义。

senses.title: Interests or fields coming together
senses.definition: to have an area of shared interest, activity or relevance with something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物拥有共同的利益、活动或相关领域
senses.example: Their research interests intersect at the study of early trade routes.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的研究兴趣在早期贸易路线研究上交汇。
senses.why: When two sets of interests overlap, the overlap is like the shared piece of two cutting outlines, so abstract concerns can intersect too.
senses.whyCN: 当两套兴趣的范围重合时，重合部分就像两个相交轮廓共有的那块区域，所以抽象的关注点也能「相交」。

senses.title: Events or conditions crossing each other
senses.definition: to cross and affect each other, especially of events, trends, or social conditions
senses.definitionCN: 相互交叉并彼此影响，多指事件、趋势或社会状况
senses.example: Poverty and poor housing intersect to shape health outcomes.
senses.exampleCN: 贫困与恶劣的住房条件相互交织，共同影响健康状况。
senses.why: If lines intersect, neither runs alone; borrowed for events, the word says that two conditions cross paths and act on the same place.
senses.whyCN: 线条相交时谁也不再单独而行；借用于事件时，表示两种状况交叉而过、作用在同一处。

senses.title: A point that is crossed by something
senses.definition: of a place, to be crossed by a road, railway, river or border
senses.definitionCN: 指某地被道路、铁路、河流或边界穿过
senses.example: The old market square is intersected by tram lines.
senses.exampleCN: 老集市广场被有轨电车线路穿过。
senses.why: This uses the passive: the road does the cutting and the place is the surface it passes through, which is the transitive image turned around.
senses.whyCN: 这里用被动语态：道路是「切」的一方，地点是被穿过的面，这正是及物画面换个方向来看。

intro.en: Intersect comes from the Latin past participle intersectus of intersecare, which joins inter and secare and passed through English Latin-style coinings.
intro.cn: intersect 来自拉丁语 intersecare 的过去分词 intersectus，由 inter 与 secare 组合，并经英语中的拉丁式构词进入英语。

items.en: The root *sek- is generally reconstructed as to cut, and it also underlies Latin secare.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语词根 *sek- 意为「切」，它也是拉丁语 secare 的来源。

items.en: Secare means to cut, cut off or divide, and it gave segmentum and sectio.
items.cn: secare 意为切、割开、分割，它生出了 segmentum 与 sectio。

items.en: Inter means between or among, and it gathers things into a shared space.
items.cn: inter 意为「在……之间」，把事物收进一个共同的空间。

items.en: Intersecare means to cut through or cut apart, and its participle intersectus supplies the English word.
items.cn: intersecare 意为「切穿、切开」，其分词 intersectus 提供了英语词形。

items.en: The verb is attested in English from the seventeenth century, first in geometry and description.
items.cn: 这个动词自十七世纪起见于英语，最初用于几何与描写。

items.en: Modern English extends the word from geometry to roads, fields and overlap of interests.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从几何扩展到道路、领域与利益的交叠。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin root secare, to cut; the near-meaning group gathers ways of crossing and meeting with a narrower reach.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁词根 secare「切」构成的一族词；近义组收「穿过、相遇」的表达，各自适用范围更窄。

entries.definition: The noun naming the point where lines or roads cross.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交点、交叉路口」，由本词加名词后缀构成。

entries.definition: A part cut off from a whole; from Latin sectio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部分、截面」，来自拉丁语 sectio，与 secare（切）同源。

entries.definition: To cut something open or apart for study, from dis- and secare.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「解剖、剖析」，由 dis- 与 secare 构成，同样保留「切」的意思。

entries.definition: To go from one side to the other; more general and often physical only.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「横过、交叉」，更一般，多限于具体动作。

entries.definition: To cover part of the same area or share part of the same range.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重叠、部分重合」，强调共享同一块区域。

entries.definition: To come nearer and finally join at a point; used of lines, paths and interests.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「汇聚、趋于一点」，多用于线条、路径与兴趣，语气偏技术。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts secare and inter, plus the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁构件 secare 与 inter，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: secare means to cut: intersect is two things cutting into each other.
normal.cn: secare 意为「切」：intersect 就是两样东西互相切入。

normal.en: inter means between or among: the cutting happens in a shared space.
normal.cn: inter 意为「在……之间」：切割发生在共同的空间里。

normal.en: The noun intersection keeps the -ion result suffix: the point left by the cutting.
normal.cn: 名词 intersection 保留表示结果的 -ion 后缀：切割留下的那个点。

normal.en: Geometry talks about two lines that intersect at a single point.
normal.cn: 几何里说两条直线交于一点。

normal.en: Compare cross: cross is the everyday word, intersect is more technical and abstract.
normal.cn: 对比 cross：cross 更日常，intersect 更偏技术、更抽象。

abstract.en: Draw an X on paper: the centre is the point where two lines cut across each other.
abstract.cn: 在纸上画一个叉：中心就是两条线互相跨过的交点。

abstract.en: Picture a blade passing through a sheet of paper: the sheet is divided into two parts.
abstract.cn: 想象刀刃穿过一张纸：纸被分成了两半。

abstract.en: See two circles staining a page, and the tiny dark patch where they overlap.
abstract.cn: 想象两个圆在纸上晕开，它们重合处那一小块颜色更深。

examples.en: These two lines intersect at the origin of the graph.
examples.cn: 这两条直线在图的原点相交。

examples.en: A narrow river intersects the farm and splits it into two plots.
examples.cn: 一条窄河横穿农场，把它分成两块地。

examples.en: Their careers intersect whenever a film and a novel share the same story.
examples.cn: 每当一部电影和一部小说讲同一个故事，他们的事业就出现交汇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引特塞克特」——「引」来两条线，「塞」进中间交叉，记作相交；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter「在……之间」+ secare「切」→ intersecare「切穿、切开」→ 过去分词 intersectus → 英语 intersect，核心义「互相切入而相遇」。

sensesIntro.en: Intersect starts with lines that cut across each other, then moves to surfaces that are cut through, areas that overlap, abstract interests and events that cross, and finally places crossed by roads.
sensesIntro.cn: intersect 先指线条互相跨过，再指把面切穿、范围重叠、抽象利益与事件交错，最后指地点被道路穿过。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines draw an X, and the small point in the middle is where they meet.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条线画出一个叉，中间那个小点就是它们相遇之处。

branches.en: THE ROAD LINE: lines and paths cut across each other, or a place is cut across by a road.
branches.cn: 道路线：线条与路径互相跨过，或某地被道路横穿。

branches.en: THE BLADE LINE: the transitive verb keeps the original cutting of a surface in two.
branches.cn: 刀锋线：及物动词保留原义「把面切成两半」。

branches.en: THE AREA LINE: two outlines that cut into each other share a region.
branches.cn: 范围线：两个互相切入的轮廓共享一块区域。

branches.en: THE ABSTRACT LINE: interests, events and conditions cross and act on the same place.
branches.cn: 抽象线：利益、事件与状况交叉而过，作用于同一处。

branches.en: Both senses keep one picture: cut across, then find something shared.
branches.cn: 义项先「跨过」，再「共享」，都保留同一幅画面。

intro.en: Intersect is built from the Latin prefix inter- and the cutting root sec-, with English -sect and -ion extending the family.
intro.cn: intersect 由拉丁语前缀 inter- 与表示「切」的词根 sec- 构成，英语再用 -sect 与 -ion 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter, secare and intersecare are all recorded, so only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter、secare 与 intersecare 均有文献记录，只有印欧语词根属于重构形式。

items.example: It marks the space where the cutting happens.
items.exampleCN: 它标出切割发生的那个空间。

items.example: The verb gives the family its cutting image.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给词族带来「切」的画面。

items.example: The compound joins inter and secare.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把 inter 与 secare 合在一起。

items.example: The participle supplies the English shape of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词分词提供了英语的词形。

items.example: The root appears in section and segment.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根见于 section 与 segment。

items.example: It marks where two roads meet on a map.
items.exampleCN: 它在地图上标出两条路相接之处。

items.example: It describes two circles that share a region.
items.exampleCN: 它形容两个共享一块区域的圆。

items.example: It forms intersection.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intersection。

items.example: The noun names the point left by the crossing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指交叉后留下的那个点。

items.meaningCN: 交叉性的；多重身份交叉的

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from inter and secare

definition_zh: 交叉点；十字路口；交集；重叠部分；交织
definition_en: the point or area where two or more lines, roads or sets cross or overlap, or the act of crossing
core_image: 两道路线在地图上交会，中心亮起一个交点标记
scene: 导航地图上，两条街道在这里汇合，中心显示一个醒目的交点。Drivers must slow down at a busy intersection like this one.
sceneCN: 这里 intersection 是「十字路口」（第 2 个义项：两条或多条道路交会处）；句意为司机在这样的繁华路口必须减速。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀还原而来，义为「相交；贯穿」
由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「交叉的；多重身份交叉的」
由 intersectional 加 -ity 构成，义为「交叉性」
由否定前缀 non- 加本词构成，义为「不相交」

senses.title: The point where lines meet
senses.definition: the point at which two or more lines, curves or surfaces cross each other
senses.definitionCN: 两条或多条直线、曲线或曲面彼此交叉的那个点
senses.example: Mark the intersection of these two straight lines on the graph.
senses.exampleCN: 在图上标出这两条直线的交点。
senses.why: Latin intersecare, to cut through, plus the result suffix -io gives a noun for the point left where the cutting lines touch.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intersecare 意为「切穿」，加上表示结果的 -io 后缀，就得到指称「切割所留之处」的名词。

senses.title: A place where roads cross
senses.definition: the place where two or more roads meet and cross, especially a junction in a town
senses.definitionCN: 两条或多条道路相遇并交叉的地方，尤指城镇中的十字路口
senses.example: The museum stands at the intersection of King Street and Market Road.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆坐落在国王街与市场路的交叉口。
senses.why: A city is drawn as lines on a map, so the geometric crossing point becomes the street corner where drivers must look both ways.
senses.whyCN: 城市被画成地图上的线条，于是几何意义上的交点变成街角，司机在那里必须左右张望。

senses.title: The shared part of two sets
senses.definition: in mathematics, the set of members that belong to all the sets being compared
senses.definitionCN: 数学中指同时属于所比较的各个集合的成员构成的集合
senses.example: The intersection of the two sets is small but not empty.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个集合的交集很小，但并不为空。
senses.why: When two outlines cut across each other they share one region, and set theory names that shared region the intersection.
senses.whyCN: 两个轮廓互相穿过时会共享一块区域，集合论就把这块共有区域称作交集。

senses.title: The overlap of abstract fields
senses.definition: the shared ground where two subjects, interests or groups touch and overlap
senses.definitionCN: 两个学科、兴趣或群体相互接触与重合的共同地带
senses.example: Her work sits at the intersection of art and climate science.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作处在艺术与气候科学的交叠处。
senses.why: The geometric point where separate lines touch becomes a metaphor for the spot where separate fields meet and produce something new.
senses.whyCN: 本来分开的线相接的那一点，被用来比喻分开的领域相遇并产生新事物的地方。

senses.title: The act of crossing or cutting
senses.definition: the action or fact of two things crossing each other or cutting across something
senses.definitionCN: 两物互相交叉或横穿某物的动作或事实
senses.example: The intersection of the beams formed a bright white patch.
senses.exampleCN: 两束光的交叉形成了一个明亮的白色光斑。
senses.why: The -io noun can name the action as well as the point, so intersection covers both the cut and its result.
senses.whyCN: -io 名词既能指结果也能指动作，所以 intersection 既指切口，也指切割这件事本身。

senses.title: Overlapping social identities
senses.definition: the overlapping of social categories such as race, gender or class to shape experience
senses.definitionCN: 种族、性别或阶层等社会范畴相互重叠，共同塑造经历
senses.example: The study examines the intersection of gender and class in factory work.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究考察工厂劳动中性别与阶层的交叉作用。
senses.why: Modern sociology reads the shared region of overlapping categories as a place of combined effects, extending the overlap sense to identity.
senses.whyCN: 现代社会把重叠范畴共享的区域理解为共同效应发生之处，把交叠义延伸到身份议题。

intro.en: Intersection is the Latin -io noun built on intersecare, to cut through, and it entered English in the seventeenth century beside the verb.
intro.cn: intersection 是建在拉丁语 intersecare「切穿」之上的 -io 名词，与动词几乎同时进入英语，见于十七世纪。

items.en: The root *sek- is generally reconstructed as to cut, and it also underlies Latin secare.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语词根 *sek- 意为「切」，它也是拉丁语 secare 的来源。

items.en: Secare means to cut or divide, and it produced sectio and segmentum.
items.cn: secare 意为切、分割，它生出了 sectio 与 segmentum。

items.en: Inter plus secare forms intersecare, to cut through, with principal parts that supply -tio endings.
items.cn: inter 加 secare 构成 intersecare，意为切穿，其变化形式提供了 -tio 词尾。

items.en: Intersectio names a cutting apart, a dividing or a point of division.
items.cn: intersectio 指切开、分割或分界之处。

items.en: The noun intersects enters English usage in the seventeenth century through learned coining.
items.cn: 名词 intersect 的衍生形式在十七世纪通过学术构词进入英语。

items.en: Modern English adds the road sense, the set-theory sense and the sociological sense.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了道路义、集合论义与社会学义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin cutting root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for crossings and meeting points.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「切」词根构成的一族词；近义组收其他表示交叉与相遇点的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to cut across each other or pass through.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「相交、贯穿」，是本词去掉名词后缀后的动词形式。

entries.definition: To cut into two equal parts, from bi- and secare.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「二等分」，由 bi- 与 secare（切）构成。

entries.definition: A part cut off from a whole; from Latin sectio.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部分、截面」，来自拉丁语 sectio，与 secare 同源。

entries.definition: A place where roads or railway lines join, often without crossing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交汇处、枢纽」，多指道路或铁路会合之处，不一定是交叉。

entries.definition: A place where two roads cross; concrete and common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「十字路口」，非常具体，多用于口语。

entries.definition: A shared area where two things partly cover the same space.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「重叠部分」，指两物部分覆盖同一空间。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts and the ordinary phrases that intersection appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁构件，以及 intersection 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: intersect is the verb: two things cut into each other.
normal.cn: intersect 是动词：两样东西互相切入。

normal.en: The -ion suffix names the result: the point left where the lines cut.
normal.cn: -ion 后缀表示结果：线条切割后留下的那个点。

normal.en: A city intersection is a small geometric diagram laid on the ground.
normal.cn: 城市的十字路口就是画在地面上的一幅小几何图。

normal.en: In set theory the intersection of two sets is what both sets contain.
normal.cn: 在集合论中，两个集合的交集就是两个集合都包含的部分。

normal.en: At the intersection of means where two fields meet and share ground.
normal.cn: at the intersection of 表示两个领域相遇、共享共同地带的所在。

abstract.en: Picture two straight roads in an aerial photo and the small crossing at their centre.
abstract.cn: 想象航拍照片里两条笔直的道路，以及它们中心那个小小的交叉。

abstract.en: Imagine stopping at a red light right on that crossing point.
abstract.cn: 想象正好停在那个交叉点上的红灯前。

abstract.en: Visualise two coloured transparent sheets lying partly on top of each other, and the darker strip between them.
abstract.cn: 想象两张彩色透明纸部分叠在一起，中间那条颜色更深的地带。

examples.en: Turn left at the next intersection and follow the signs to the harbour.
examples.cn: 在下一个路口左转，沿着路标前往港口。

examples.en: The intersection of the two circles is that crescent-shaped area.
examples.cn: 两个圆的交叉部分就是那块月牙形的区域。

examples.en: Their research lies at the intersection of medicine and engineering.
examples.cn: 他们的研究处在医学与工程学的交叠处。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特塞克」——「因」为两条线「塞」到一起才「克」出交点：交点、路口；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter「在……之间」+ secare「切」→ intersecare「切穿」→ intersectio「分割、交点」→ 英语 intersection，核心义「切割相会之处」。

sensesIntro.en: Intersection moves from the geometric point where lines cut, to the street corner, to the shared part of sets, to overlapping fields, the act of crossing, and overlapping identities.
sensesIntro.cn: intersection 从线条切割处的几何点，走向街口、集合的共有部分、领域重叠、交叉动作，直到身份交叠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two roads meet on a map and a small dot marks their crossing.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上两条路相接，一个小点标出它们的交叉处。

branches.en: THE GEOMETRY LINE: the point and the act of lines cutting across each other.
branches.cn: 几何线：线条互相切割所留下的点与这个动作本身。

branches.en: THE STREET LINE: the geometric point set on the ground becomes a junction of roads.
branches.cn: 街道线：几何点落在地面上，变成道路的交会处。

branches.en: THE SET LINE: overlapping outlines share one region, which mathematics names.
branches.cn: 集合线：重叠的轮廓共享一块区域，数学为它命名。

branches.en: THE FIELD LINE: separate subjects meet at a point that produces something new.
branches.cn: 领域线：分开的学科在一点相遇，于是产生新东西。

branches.en: THE IDENTITY LINE: categories of race, gender and class overlap and combine.
branches.cn: 身份线：种族、性别与阶层等范畴重叠并共同作用。

intro.en: Intersection is the Latin -io noun of intersecare, built from inter-, the root sec-, and the result suffix -ion.
intro.cn: intersection 是 intersecare 的拉丁 -io 名词，由 inter-、词根 sec- 与表示结果的 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter, secare and intersecare are all recorded; intersectio belongs to later learned Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter、secare 与 intersecare 均有记录；intersectio 属于后期学术拉丁语。

items.example: It locates the cutting in a shared space.
items.exampleCN: 它把切割放在一个共同的空间里。

items.example: The verb supplies the cutting image.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「切」的画面。

items.example: It joins inter and secare into one action.
items.exampleCN: 它把 inter 与 secare 合成一个动作。

items.example: The root recurs in section and bisect.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根见于 section 与 bisect。

items.example: It turns the cutting act into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把切割动作变成名词。

items.example: Two intersections share a northbound lane on this route.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线上的两个路口共用一条北行车道。

items.example: The verb states what produces the intersection.
items.exampleCN: 动词说明是什么造成了这个交点。

items.example: It forms intersectional.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intersectional。

items.example: Modern sociology asks intersectional questions.
items.exampleCN: 现代社会学会提出交叉性的问题。

items.example: It forms intersectionality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intersectionality。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from inter and secare

definition_zh: 交织；缠绕；紧密相连；使缠绕
definition_en: to twist or twine two or more things together so that they become closely woven or linked
core_image: 两股藤蔓相互绕转，缠成一束再也分不开的辫子
scene: 花园里，两株牵牛花的藤蔓沿着同一根竹竿向上爬。The vines intertwine around the bamboo pole and climb toward the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 intertwine 是「缠绕、交织」（第 1 个义项：藤蔓或线绳彼此绕转）；句意为藤蔓缠绕着竹竿，朝着阳光向上攀爬。

collocations.zh: 难分难解地交织在一起

derivatives.zh: 过去分词作形容词，义为「交织的；紧密相连的」
现在分词作名词，义为「交织、缠绕」
由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「交织的状态」（较少见）

senses.title: Vines or threads twisting together
senses.definition: to twist or wind two or more plants, threads or strands around each other
senses.definitionCN: 把两株或多株植物、多根线、多股绳彼此绕来绕去
senses.example: The two vines intertwine around the iron gate.
senses.exampleCN: 两条藤蔓绕在铁门上，缠在一起。
senses.why: Twine comes from Old English twin, doubled thread, so intertwine is twining two threads into each other, the most concrete image of the family.
senses.whyCN: twine 源自英语 twin「双股的线」，所以 intertwine 就是把两根线彼此缠绕，这是整个词族中最具体的画面。

senses.title: Bodies or hands clasping
senses.definition: to hold or press together with limbs or fingers crossing or interlacing
senses.definitionCN: 四肢或手指交叉缠绕地抱在一起或握在一起
senses.example: Their fingers intertwine as they walk along the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们沿河散步时十指相扣。
senses.why: The same twisting picture applied to bodies gives the image of limbs woven together, as strands of a rope are.
senses.whyCN: 把同样的绕转画面用在身体上，就得到肢体像绳股一样编在一起的意象。

senses.title: Things closely connected and hard to separate
senses.titleCN: 事物紧密相连、难分难解
senses.definition: of ideas, events or processes, to be so closely connected that they cannot easily be separated
senses.definitionCN: 指观念、事件或过程联系极为紧密，难以轻易分开
senses.example: Economic growth and urban migration are closely intertwined.
senses.exampleCN: 经济增长与城市化迁移紧密交织。
senses.why: Once two strands are twisted into one cord, pulling one pulls the other, so intertwined comes to mean inseparably connected.
senses.whyCN: 两股线一旦扭成一根绳，拉一股就带动另一股，于是 intertwined 引申为「难分难解的联系」。

senses.title: To twist things into one another
senses.definition: to cause two or more things to be twisted or wound round each other
senses.definitionCN: 使两样或多样的东西彼此绕转、缠在一起
senses.example: She intertwined the ribbons to make a wreath.
senses.exampleCN: 她把丝带绞缠在一起，做成一个花环。
senses.why: In the transitive use the hand does the twisting, so the verb names the act of making one strand out of several.
senses.whyCN: 在及物用法中，是手在做「绞」的动作，因此动词指的是把几股并成一股的那件事。

senses.title: Stories or paths crossing each other
senses.definition: of stories, plots or routes, to cross and wind through each other
senses.definitionCN: 指故事、情节或路线相互交叉、蜿蜒穿行
senses.example: The plot lines intertwine before the final reunion.
senses.exampleCN: 几条情节线在最终重逢之前相互交织。
senses.why: Two paths that wind through each other look like two threads in a braid, so a narrative can be described as intertwining.
senses.whyCN: 两条路线蜿蜒穿行、彼此交错，看起来就像辫子里的两股线，所以叙事也能用「交织」来形容。

senses.title: Worlds or lives sharing a fate
senses.definition: of lives, cultures or worlds, to become deeply mixed and mutually involved
senses.definitionCN: 指生活、文化或世界深度融合、彼此牵连
senses.example: Since the move, our lives have intertwined more than ever.
senses.exampleCN: 自从搬家以来，我们的生活比以往任何时候都更加交融。
senses.why: The physical winding grows into a portrait of two lives that wind around each other and cannot easily be untangled.
senses.whyCN: 有形的缠绕延伸为两个人生互相绕转、难以解开的写照。

intro.en: Intertwine is an English compound of inter-, between, and twine, a cord of two threads, whose origin is twin, the number two.
intro.cn: intertwine 是英语复合词，由 inter-（在……之间）与 twine（双股绳）构成，而 twine 的来源是 twin「两个」。

items.en: The root *dwo- is the general source of two and twin; the underlying *dwi- is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: *dwo- 是 two 与 twin 的普遍来源，更早的 *dwi- 属于重构形式。

items.en: Twin means a pair, and twine describes double thread.
items.cn: twin 意为成对，twine 指双股的线。

items.en: The verb twine develops the sense to twist two strands, and modern twine names a doubled cord.
items.cn: 动词 twine 发展出「扭两股线」的意思，现代 twine 指合股绳。

items.en: Intersect-style compounds with inter- were coined freely, and intertwine is usually dated to the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语自由地用 inter- 造出这类复合词，intertwine 一般认为出现在十六世纪。

items.en: The literal winding extends to abstract lives, arguments and ideas in modern usage.
items.cn: 现代用法把有形的缠绕扩展到抽象的人生、论辩与观念。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on twin and twine; the near-meaning group gathers ways of twisting and binding that differ in strength.
note.cn: 形近组收由 twin 与 twine 构成的一族词；近义组收扭转、系绑类表达，彼此强度不同。

entries.definition: Strong string made of two or more strands twisted together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「双股绳」，即由两股或多股扭成结实的绳子，是本词的构词基础。

entries.definition: One of two children born together, or forming a matching pair.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「双胞胎、成对的」，是 twine 的来源词。

entries.definition: To bend or turn something with a twisting motion; it is only look-alike in its tw- start and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「扭转」，只是开头 tw- 形似，词源不同。

entries.definition: To weave things over and under each other, usually of threads or facts.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「交织、穿插」，强调经纬式交错，多指丝线与事实。

entries.definition: To wind or twist around something, often used of arms or plants.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缠住、环绕」，常用于手臂或植物。

entries.definition: To become twisted into a confused mass; implies disorder, unlike intertwine.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缠结、纠缠」，暗含杂乱，与表达整齐交缠的 intertwine 不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real parts twin and twine, plus the phrases that intertwine appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的构件 twin 与 twine，以及 intertwine 实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: twin means two: intertwine starts from the idea of a doubled thread.
normal.cn: twin 意为「两个」：intertwine 就从双股线的观念出发。

normal.en: twine is a cord of two strands twisted; the verb twines things together.
normal.cn: twine 是由两股扭成的绳；动词 twine 就是把东西扭到一起。

normal.en: inter- puts the twisting between two things, so neither stands alone.
normal.cn: inter- 表示缠绕发生在两者之间，所以谁也不再单独而立。

normal.en: In modern usage things become closely intertwined, so they cannot be pulled apart.
normal.cn: 现代用法里事物变得紧密相连，再也拉不开。

normal.en: Compare interweave: weaving goes over and under, intertwining goes round and round.
normal.cn: 对比 interweave：编织是上下穿插，缠绕是绕着转圈。

abstract.en: Picture two green vine shoots climbing the same pole and winding round each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两根绿色藤蔓爬上同一根竹竿，彼此绕着转圈。

abstract.en: Think of ten fingers locked together and turned to face the other person.
abstract.cn: 想到十根手指相扣，转过来面向对方。

abstract.en: See a thick rope of red and blue fibres, where the two colours run side by side to the end.
abstract.cn: 想到一根红蓝纤维绞成的粗绳，两种颜色并排一直延伸到端头。

examples.en: Ivy has intertwined with the fence so thickly that nothing can pass through.
examples.cn: 常春藤与栅栏交织得密不透风，什么东西都穿不过去。

examples.en: The two families are intertwined by marriage and by business.
examples.cn: 这两个家族通过婚姻和生意紧密相连。

examples.en: She wore a ring of intertwined silver wires.
examples.cn: 她戴着一枚银线交织而成的戒指。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特推因」——「推」来「因」为两条线互相绕，编在一起：交织、缠绕；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语 inter-「在……之间」+ twine「双股绳」；twine 又与 twin「成双」同源，源于原始印欧语 *dwo-「二」，核心义「两股彼此绕成一股」。

sensesIntro.en: Intertwine begins with vines and threads wound together, then moves to clasped limbs, inseparable ideas, the act of twisting, crossing stories, and lives that share a fate.
sensesIntro.cn: intertwine 从藤蔓与线绳绕在一起开始，延伸到相扣的肢体、难分的事物、绞缠的动作、交错的情节，以及同命相连的人生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two vines wind round one pole and become one thick braid.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根藤蔓绕同一根杆子，缠成一根粗辫。

branches.en: THE HAND LINE: the literal twisting of threads, vines and ribbons, including the act itself.
branches.cn: 手工线：线、藤与丝带的有形扭转，也包括这个动作本身。

branches.en: THE BODY LINE: fingers and limbs interlace like strands of rope.
branches.cn: 身体线：手指与四肢像绳股一样互相穿插。

branches.en: THE BINDING LINE: what is woven together cannot be pulled apart by pulling one thread.
branches.cn: 联结线：编在一起的东西，拉一股就带不动另一股。

branches.en: THE STORY LINE: plots and routes wind through each other like two paths.
branches.cn: 叙事线：情节与路线像两条小路那样彼此穿行。

branches.en: THE LIFE LINE: two lives wind around each other and share a fate.
branches.cn: 人生线：两个人的人生互相绕转，共担命运。

intro.en: Intertwine is an English compound built from the prefix inter- and the noun twine; the relatives twine and twin carry the idea of two.
intro.cn: intertwine 是英语复合词，由前缀 inter- 与名词 twine 构成；同族词 twine 与 twin 都带「二」的观念。

latinIntro.en: The prefix inter- is Latin, but twine is Germanic, so the word mixes a Latin prefix with an Old English root; latinEntries holds the prefix only.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 inter- 来自拉丁语，而 twine 属于日耳曼语，所以这个词是拉丁前缀接古英语词根；拉丁同源部分只有这个前缀。

items.example: The prefix says the twisting happens between two things.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示缠绕发生在两者之间。

items.example: Twin supplies the idea of two.
items.exampleCN: twin 提供「二」的观念。

items.example: Twine is the strand that is twisted.
items.exampleCN: twine 就是被扭起来的那股线。

items.example: The verb twine already means to twist.
items.exampleCN: 动词 twine 本身已有「扭」的意思。

items.example: The movement of the plot intertwines with the changing season.
items.exampleCN: 情节的推进与季节的更替相互交织。

items.example: The results are intertwined and cannot be studied apart.
items.exampleCN: 这些结果紧密交织，无法分开研究。

items.example: It forms intertwining.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intertwining。

items.example: It forms intertwinement, which is rare and formal.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intertwinement，这个形式罕见且正式。

items.example: Interweave uses the same prefix with weaving.
items.exampleCN: interweave 用同一前缀表示「编织」。

items.meaning: in the space separating two things
items.example: Between and entwine carry the same two-sided idea.
items.exampleCN: between 与 entwine 都带「两边之间」的观念。

definition_zh: 亲密；亲近；（语言或风格的）亲切感；（委婉）私密之事
definition_en: a close, warm, personal connection that lets people share private feelings and weak spots
core_image: 两人凑得很近，低声说话，把最里层的心事给对方看
scene: 冬夜的厨房里只剩两个人，火光把脸照得很近。Years of shared dinners gave the sisters an easy intimacy.
sceneCN: 这里 intimacy 是「亲密关系」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间亲近、可以互说心事的关系）；句意为多年一起吃饭让姐妹之间有了自然的亲密感。图中可辨识物件：炉火、两只茶杯、窗上的霜花。

pos.zh: 名词：亲密；亲近；亲切感；（委婉）私密之事

collocations.phrase: the intimacy of a small cafe

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词词尾回溯而成，义为「亲密的；私下的；内心的」
与本词同源但走「告知」一线，义为「暗示；通告」
由 intimate 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「亲密地；详尽地」
由 intimate 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「亲密程度」

senses.title: A close personal bond
senses.definition: a close, affectionate relationship in which people can be open with one another
senses.definitionCN: 亲近而温暖的关系，彼此可以坦诚相待
senses.example: The long walk home built an unexpected intimacy between them.
senses.exampleCN: 一起走回家的长路在他们之间生出意想不到的亲密。
senses.why: Latin intimus is the innermost of all, so intimacy is the closeness that reaches the very center of a person rather than the surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intimus 意为「最里层的」，所以亲密是走到一个人最深处、而非停留在表面的靠近。

senses.title: The value of keeping things private
senses.definition: the quality of something being deeply personal and shielded from strangers
senses.definitionCN: 某事物属于个人深处、不让外人看见的性质
senses.example: The intimacy of the diary made her hesitate to show it to anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 这本日记太私密，她犹豫着谁都不愿给看。
senses.why: What lies innermost is naturally kept from general view, so the invented noun turns being innermost into a quality of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 最里层的东西天然不对外公开，于是这个后起的名词把「身处最里」变成了事物本身的属性。

senses.title: Warmth in a place or an atmosphere
senses.titleCN: 亲切感；局促而温馨的氛围
senses.definition: a warm, private, enveloping quality of a place, room, voice, or style
senses.definitionCN: 场所、房间、声音或文体带给人的温暖、贴身而私密的感受
senses.example: The intimacy of the candle-lit room encouraged everyone to speak honestly.
senses.exampleCN: 烛光房间的亲切感让大家愿意说出真心话。
senses.why: The same inner closeness felt between people can also be felt between a person and a space, a voice, or a manner of writing.
senses.whyCN: 人与人之间的那种靠近，也能发生在人与空间、声音或文风之间。

senses.title: Sexual closeness
senses.definition: sexual contact or sexual closeness, usually mentioned in polite or cautious language
senses.definitionCN: 性接触或性方面的亲近，用语通常委婉谨慎
senses.example: The novel treats physical intimacy with great tenderness.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说以极大的温柔处理身体上的亲密。
senses.why: The most private closeness of all came to stand politely for sexual closeness, often joined with physical.
senses.whyCN: 最私密的靠近在礼貌语境中转而指性接触，而且常与 physical 连用。

senses.title: Deep knowledge of something
senses.definition: a deep, detailed understanding of a subject or a field, as in careful acquaintance with it
senses.definitionCN: 对某一主题或领域的深入、细致的了解
senses.example: Her intimacy with the old maps was obvious from the first question.
senses.exampleCN: 从第一个问题就能看出她对那些旧地图的熟稔。
senses.why: To know something intimately is to have gone past its surface to its center, so intimacy also names close acquaintance with knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 深入认识一件事就是越过它的表面抵达核心，因此亲密也指对知识的熟稔。

senses.title: A private detail, often in the plural
senses.definition: a small personal detail about someone, especially one disclosed in a private setting
senses.definitionCN: 关于某人的细小私事，尤指私下才说出来的
senses.example: Over years of friendship, they exchanged small intimacies about their families.
senses.exampleCN: 多年友谊中，她们交换着各自家庭的小小私事。
senses.why: The private is countable too: each innermost detail one lets out is one of the intimacies of that person.
senses.whyCN: 「私密」也能一件件数：每吐露一件最里层的事，就成为那个人的一件私事。

senses.title: Unwelcome closeness
senses.titleCN: 过分亲近；私密而令人不安
senses.definition: an unwelcome intrusion into private space or private knowledge, as in phrases warning that something is an intimacy
senses.definitionCN: 对私人空间的侵扰，或过分触及隐私，短语中常带不满或警惕
senses.example: Some viewers felt the cameras pushed intimacy past the point of decency.
senses.exampleCN: 一些观众觉得摄像头把近距离变成了对隐私的冒犯。
senses.why: Pushing closeness past its proper line turns the warm inner touch into an intrusion, which is the shadow of the same core image.
senses.whyCN: 把靠近推过合适的界线，温暖的内在触碰就变成侵扰，这是同一核心意象的阴暗面。

intro.en: Intimacy grew out of the adjective intimate, which descends from Latin intimus, the innermost point of a thing, through a sixteenth-century borrowing.
intro.cn: intimacy 由形容词 intimate 派生，而 intimate 在十六世纪借自拉丁语 intimus（某物最里的部分）。

items.en: The preposition in and a superlative ending of place combine to form the adjective intimus, the inmost or deepest part of something.
items.cn: 介词 in 与表示地点的最高级词尾合成形容词 intimus，意为「最内的、最深处的」。

items.en: The noun intimatus means a close friendship, and the related verb intimare means to bring inside or to announce. The friendship noun is the ancestor of the English word.
items.cn: 名词 intimatus 意为「亲密的友谊」，相关动词 intimare 意为「带进里面、宣告」；其中「友谊」义才是英语词的祖先。

items.en: Late Latin applies the innermost adjective to persons, so that an intimate friend is literally the friend nearest the center.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语把人纳入「最里」的用法：亲密的朋友字面上就是离中心最近的朋友。

items.en: English borrows the adjective as intimate, meaning close in personal feeling, and its relatives carry the idea of closeness into speech and writing.
items.cn: 英语借入形容词 intimate，表示情感上的亲近，相关词形也把「靠近」带入说话与书写。

items.en: Intimacy appears as a noun in the seventeenth century, built on the English adjective with the suffix -cy, which turns an adjective into a quality.
items.cn: intimacy 作为名词于十七世纪出现，由英语形容词加后缀 -cy 构成，把形容词变成抽象性质。

items.en: The word spreads from friendship to atmosphere, then to polite references to sexual closeness, and finally to deep acquaintance with a subject.
items.cn: 这个词从友谊扩展到氛围，再用于对性亲密的委婉表达，最后指对某一领域的深入认识。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on Latin intimus; the near-meaning group gathers names for closeness that differ in warmth, depth and grammatical shape.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语 intimus 这一词根上的词；近义组收各种表示「靠近」的名词，温度、深浅和词形各不相同。

entries.definition: Close, private, or deeply personal; the adjective from which the noun is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「亲密的、私下的、内心深处的」，本词正是由它构成。

entries.definition: In a close and personal way, or thoroughly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「亲密地；透彻地」。

entries.definition: A hint or an indirect signal, from the announcing line of the Latin family rather than the friendship line.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「暗示、通告」，来自这一族拉丁词中的「告知」一线，而非「友谊」一线。

entries.definition: To frighten someone into doing something; it looks similar but comes from timidus, meaning fearful.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「恐吓、胁迫」；只是拼写相近，实际来自 timidus（胆怯的），词源不同。

entries.definition: A general state of being near, in space or in feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接近、亲近」，可指空间也可指情感，比本词更笼统。

entries.definition: The state of knowing someone or something well; colder than the warmth of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「熟悉、熟识」，强调知道得多，不强调温情。

entries.definition: A relationship between people who like and support each other, but not necessarily a deeply private one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「友谊」，指互相喜欢和支持的关系，但不一定私密到交心。

entries.definition: A feeling of fondness; it stresses love and gentleness rather than private closeness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喜爱、感情」，强调爱意与温柔，而不是私密的靠近。

entries.definition: The state of being kept hidden from others; it looks at the outside eye rather than the inner bond.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「保密、隐秘」，着眼的是不让外人知道，而非两人之间的纽带。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the real Latin root intimus and the collocations the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的拉丁词根 intimus，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Intimus is the innermost point: intimacy is closeness that reaches all the way inside.
normal.cn: intimus 意为「最里的那一点」：intimacy 就是一直抵达内部的靠近。

normal.en: The adjective intimate came first; the noun intimacy was built on it with the suffix -cy.
normal.cn: 先有形容词 intimate，再在它后面加后缀 -cy 造出名词 intimacy。

normal.en: Shared secrets build intimacy; a stranger may know your name but never that inner layer.
normal.cn: 交换秘密会建立亲密感；陌生人也许知道你的名字，却碰不到那层内里。

normal.en: The intimacy of a small cafe comes from size: the smaller the space, the closer everyone sits.
normal.cn: 小咖啡馆的亲切感来自尺寸：空间越小，人坐得越近。

normal.en: Compare intimate and intimidate: only the second one has the d of dread.
normal.cn: 对比 intimate 与 intimidate：只有后者带着表示「恐惧」的字母 d。

abstract.en: Picture two people at a kitchen table, speaking in a low voice: the bond that makes whispering natural is the intimacy.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人在餐桌边低声说话：让低声细语变得自然的那种纽带，就是 intimacy。

abstract.en: Think of a diary with a tiny lock: what the lock keeps innermost is the intimacy of the pages.
abstract.cn: 想象一本带小锁的日记：锁守住的最里层，就是日记页面的私密。

abstract.en: Imagine a candle-lit room that seems to shrink around you: the room seems to wrap you in closeness.
abstract.cn: 想象一间被烛光照亮的房间，仿佛在你身边收拢：房间像用亲近把你裹住。

examples.en: Shared meals and long talks gradually turned neighbours into friends with real intimacy.
examples.cn: 一起吃饭和长谈，让邻居慢慢变成真正亲密的友人。

examples.en: Critics praised the intimacy of the film, which felt like a conversation in a quiet room.
examples.cn: 评论称赞这部电影的亲切感，像在一间安静的房间里对话。

examples.en: The letter described a few small intimacies of village life.
examples.cn: 这封信描述了乡村生活的一些小小私事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因提密兮」——离得近、说得密，只因两人交心；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intimus 意为「最内的、最深处的」，由 in（在内）加地点最高级词尾构成；同族名词 intimatus 意为「亲密的友谊」。英语于十六世纪借入形容词 intimate，十七世纪再由它加后缀 -cy 造出名词 intimacy。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses all keep the same core of reaching the inner layer: a bond between people, the private quality of a thing, an atmosphere, sexual closeness, deep knowledge, a disclosed detail, and closeness that has gone too far.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项共用同一个内核，即抵达最里层：人与人之间的纽带、事物的私密性质、场所氛围、性亲密、深入的知识、被吐露的私事，以及越界的靠近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people sit very close, heads together, telling each other the things kept deepest inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人挨得很近，头凑在一起，互说藏在最深处的那些事。

branches.en: THE BOND: closeness between people is the plainest sense of the word.
branches.cn: 纽带线：人与人之间的靠近是这个词最朴素的义项。

branches.en: THE PRIVATE LAYER: what is innermost is shielded, and its smallest details can be counted.
branches.cn: 私密层：最里层的东西被护住，而其中最小的细节可以一件件数出来。

branches.en: THE ROOM: a place, a voice or a style can wrap a listener in the same closeness.
branches.cn: 房间线：场所、声音或文体也能用同样的靠近把人裹住。

branches.en: THE POLITE SHADE: the most private closeness becomes the cautious name for sexual closeness.
branches.cn: 委婉线：最私密的靠近成为对性亲密的谨慎说法。

branches.en: THE TWO EDGES: deep acquaintance with a subject sits at one edge, and closeness pushed too far at the other.
branches.cn: 两极线：一端是对某领域的深入认识，另一端是推得过远的靠近。

intro.en: Intimacy is a Latin-rooted noun: the root marks what is innermost, and the English suffix -cy turns that quality into an abstract noun.
intro.cn: intimacy 是拉丁词根构成的名词：词根标示「最里层」，英语后缀 -cy 把这性质变为抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin intimus is a superlative of place, and Latin already had a noun intimatus for close friendship.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intimus 是表示地点的最高级，拉丁语本身已有名词 intimatus 表示亲密友谊。

items.example: The prefix locates the quality inside a thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把这种性质定位到事物的内部。

items.example: The ending marks the extreme degree of being inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标示「在最里面」的最高程度。

items.example: Intimus supplies the core of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: intimus 提供整个词族的核心。

items.example: The Latin noun is the direct ancestor of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是英语名词的直接祖先。

items.example: The English adjective came first by borrowing.
items.exampleCN: 英语形容词先由借词形成。

items.example: The suffix -cy turns intimate into intimacy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 把 intimate 变成 intimacy。

items.example: It forms intimately from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它由形容词构成 intimately。

items.example: It forms intimateness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intimateness。

items.example: It appears in intimation, the hinting word.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在表示「暗示」的 intimation 中。

latinEntries.example: Intimus sits at the center of the family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: intimus 位于这一词族的中心。

latinEntries.example: The noun names a friendship nearest the inner circle.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个名词指最接近内圈的友谊。

latinEntries.example: The verb gives the announcing line of the family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词给出这一词族中「告知」的一线。

latinEntries.example: The adverb keeps the same innermost idea in Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个副词在拉丁语中保留同样的「最里层」含义。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词词尾回溯而成，义为「亲密的；私下的；内心的」
与本词同源但走「告知」一线，义为「暗示；通告」
由 intimate 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「亲密地；详尽地」
由 intimate 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「亲密程度」

definition_zh: 恐吓；威胁；使胆怯；使畏缩
definition_en: to frighten someone, especially with threats or a show of force, so that they feel small and give way
core_image: 高大的身影把人逼到墙角，对方声音发抖、往后缩
scene: 巷口的路灯坏了，高大的男人拦住小店老板，压低声音说话。Thugs tried to intimidate the shopkeeper so that no one would report them.
sceneCN: 这里 intimidate 是「恐吓、威胁」（第 1 个义项：用威胁或气势让对方害怕而让步）；句意为恶棍试图恐吓店主，好让谁也不敢告发他们。图中可辨识物件：坏掉的路灯、关了一半的卷帘门、墙角。

pos.zh: 动词：恐吓；威胁；使胆怯；使畏缩

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「恐吓；威胁」
由本词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「令人胆怯的；令人望而生畏的」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「被吓住的；感到胆怯的」
由本词加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「恐吓者」
由本词加形容词后缀 -atory（借自 -ion）构成，义为「带恐吓性质的」，多用于法律语境

senses.title: To frighten someone into compliance
senses.definition: to frighten someone, especially by threats or force, so that they become unwilling to act or resist
senses.definitionCN: 用威胁或武力使人害怕，从而不敢行动或反抗
senses.example: The staff claimed that managers intimidated them into working unpaid hours.
senses.exampleCN: 员工称经理恐吓他们无偿加班。
senses.why: Latin timidus is fearful, and the verb makes someone fearful, so the core image is another person being reduced to timidity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 timidus 意为「胆怯的」，这个动词就是把别人变得胆怯，核心意象是让人缩回去。

senses.title: To make someone feel small or unconfident
senses.titleCN: 使胆怯；使感到自己渺小
senses.definition: to make someone feel nervous, inferior, or unable to perform, often without any threat at all
senses.definitionCN: 使人紧张、自卑或发挥失常，往往并不需要真的威胁
senses.example: A row of silent judges can intimidate even a seasoned speaker.
senses.exampleCN: 一排沉默的评委就能让老练的讲者发怵。
senses.why: Threats are not the only way to create fear; a grand setting or a cold silence can make a person feel timid all by itself.
senses.whyCN: 制造恐惧不一定要真的威胁；宏大的场面或冰冷的沉默本身就足以让人胆怯。

senses.title: To deter by force, as a tactic
senses.definition: to use threats, violence, or displays of strength in order to deter someone from an action
senses.definitionCN: 用威胁、暴力或武力展示来阻止某人采取行动
senses.example: Soldiers were sent to intimidate the villagers and stop them from voting.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵被派去震慑村民，阻止他们投票。
senses.why: The fear is deliberately aimed: the point is not to hurt someone but to frighten them so thoroughly that they stay still.
senses.whyCN: 这种恐惧是被刻意瞄准的：目的不在伤害，而在于把人吓住，让人不敢动。

senses.title: To be overawed by something grand
senses.definition: to be made to feel humble or afraid by the size, difficulty, or authority of something, often in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 被事物的规模、难度或权威压得自觉渺小或害怕，常用被动形式
senses.example: She felt intimidated by the sheer size of the library catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 光是那份图书馆目录的规模就让她望而生畏。
senses.why: When the object is huge enough, no person has to threaten anyone: size and difficulty do the frightening on their own.
senses.whyCN: 当对象足够庞大时，不需要任何人来威胁：规模与难度本身就在吓人。

senses.title: To coerce by unlawful threats
senses.definition: in law, to compel someone to act or refrain from acting through unlawful threats or intimidation
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指用非法威胁或恐吓迫使某人作为或不作为
senses.example: The union is accused of intimidating workers who refused to join the strike.
senses.exampleCN: 该工会被控恐吓拒绝参加罢工的工人。
senses.why: Law takes the everyday fear and gives it a name as a wrong: forcing a will by fear is itself an offence.
senses.whyCN: 法律把日常的恐惧定为一种过错：用恐惧迫使他人屈服本身就构成违法。

senses.title: In the older sense of inspiring fear
senses.titleCN: （古旧语境）使人畏惧；作为骇人的存在
senses.definition: in older usage, to inspire fear or awe by itself, rather than to frighten a particular person into something
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法中指本身令人畏惧或敬畏，而非使某个人屈服
senses.example: The old tales say a dragon intimidated the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的传说称，一条龙让整个山谷都畏惧。
senses.why: Before the modern focus on causing someone to give way, the verb could simply mean to look or be frightening.
senses.whyCN: 在现代「使人屈服」这一重点之前，这个动词只表示看上去令人害怕或本身骇人。

intro.en: Intimidate comes from Latin through French: the Latin word for fear supplies the stem, and the verb ending tells you it is an act performed on someone.
intro.cn: intimidate 经由法语来自拉丁语：拉丁语中表示「害怕」的词提供词根，词尾表明这是施加于人身上的行为。

items.en: The adjective timidus means fearful or timid, and it rests on the noun timor, fear.
items.cn: 形容词 timidus 意为「胆怯的」，其基础是名词 timor「恐惧」。

items.en: Medieval Latin forms the verb intimidare on the adjective timidus, adding the verb element -are so that it means to make someone afraid. The origin of the initial syllable is not fully settled.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语在形容词 timidus 上加动词成分 -are 构成 intimidare，意为「使人害怕」；开头音节的来源尚无定论。

items.en: French carries the verb onward as intimider, keeping the notion of putting fear into a person.
items.cn: 法语以 intimider 延续这个动词，保留「把恐惧放进人心里」的含义。

items.en: English borrows it as intimidate in the seventeenth century, used especially of frightening someone into doing something.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入 intimidate，尤指把某人吓得去做某事。

items.en: The word spreads from a vague sense of frightening to concrete threats, to the legal offence of coercing a will, and to feeling small.
items.cn: 这个词从笼统的「吓人」扩展到具体威胁、法律上的胁迫罪，以及「使人自觉渺小」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin root for fear; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of frightening and pressuring that differ in intent and force.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「恐惧」词根上的词；近义组收恐吓与施压类动词，用意和力度各不相同。

entries.definition: Shy and easily frightened; the adjective sits at the root of the whole family.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「胆怯的、羞怯的」，正是这一词族的词根形容词。

entries.definition: The quality of being timid or easily frightened.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胆怯、羞怯」，指容易害怕的性质。

entries.definition: The act or crime of frightening someone into doing or not doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恐吓、胁迫」，由本词加后缀直接构成。

entries.definition: Close and private; it begins with the same letters but comes from intimus, the innermost point.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「亲密的、私下的」；开头字母相同，但来自 intimus（最里面），词源不同。

entries.definition: Literary adjective for fearful; it shares the fear root with the target word.
entries.definitionCN: 文学的「胆小的」形容词，与目标词共享「恐惧」词根。

entries.definition: To make someone afraid; general, and without the aim of forcing a person to give way.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使害怕」，最通用，不强调逼人屈服。

entries.definition: To say that harm will come if someone does not do what you want; the threats are spoken.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「威胁」，强调把伤害说出口来逼迫对方。

entries.definition: To frighten or hurt someone weaker, usually repeatedly; close to the everyday sense of intimidation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欺凌」，多指反复欺负弱者，接近恐吓的日常义。

entries.definition: To force someone by threats or pressure; formal and legal, with the same forcing result.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强迫、胁迫」，语气正式，多用于法律，结果与恐吓相同。

entries.definition: To make someone lose courage, as a difficult task does; closer to the feeling of being overawed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使气馁、使胆怯」，多因任务艰难而言，更接近「被镇住」的义项。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin fear root and the collocations the verb actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的拉丁语「恐惧」词根，以及这个动词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: The stem is tim, the fear in timid: intimidate means to put tim inside another person.
normal.cn: 词干是 tim，就是 timid 里的那点「怕」：intimidate 就是把这份怕塞进别人心里。

normal.en: The ending -ate makes it an action done to someone, not a description.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ate 使它成为一个施加于人的动作，而不是一种描述。

normal.en: A witness who is intimidated goes quiet, so the phrase is intimidated into silence.
normal.cn: 证人一旦被恐吓就会闭嘴，所以有 intimidated into silence 这种说法。

normal.en: The adjective intimidating describes the source of the fear, the person or task that does the scaring.
normal.cn: 形容词 intimidating 描述恐惧的来源，也就是吓人的那个人或那件事。

normal.en: Compare timid and intimidate: the timid person feels the fear, the intimidator plants it.
normal.cn: 对比 timid 与 intimidate：胆怯的人承受恐惧，恐吓者把恐惧种下去。

abstract.en: Picture a tall figure standing over a small one, casting a shadow that keeps growing: the shadow is the fear being poured in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个高大的身影压住一个矮小的身影，投下的影子越拉越长：那影子就是被灌进去的恐惧。

abstract.en: Think of a scale: the one who threatens presses down hard until the other side cannot lift its head.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平：恐吓者重重压下一头，直到另一端抬不起头。

abstract.en: A giant library door can intimidate without a single word: size alone can make a person feel tiny.
abstract.cn: 一扇巨大的图书馆门一言不发也能让人发怵：光是尺度就能把人压小。

examples.en: The coach never shouted at players, preferring to encourage them rather than intimidate them.
examples.cn: 教练从不对球员吼叫，宁可鼓励也不愿恐吓他们。

examples.en: Many first-year students feel intimidated by the lecture halls.
examples.cn: 许多新生被讲堂的气派镇住而感到胆怯。

examples.en: He was charged with intimidation after secretly following a witness home.
examples.cn: 他因暗中跟踪一名证人回家而以恐吓罪名被起诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因提米逮他」——先让人害怕，再趁机下手；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 timor（恐惧）与其形容词 timidus（胆怯的）是词根，中世纪拉丁语加动词词尾构成 intimidare（使人害怕），经法语 intimider 于十七世纪进入英语。词根 tim- 只表示「怕」，与表示「最里面」的 intim- 不是同一来源。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all apply the same fear root: outright threats, a cold setting that makes a person feel small, force used to deter others, being awed by something grand, the legal offence of coercing a will, and the older sense of simply being frightening.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都在使用同一个「恐惧」词根：直接的威胁、让人自觉渺小的冷漠场面、用来震慑他人的武力、被宏大事物镇住、法律上的胁迫罪，以及古旧语境中「本身骇人」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large figure backs a smaller one into a corner, and the smaller one shrinks and goes quiet.
core.cn: 核心意象：高大的身影把矮小的人逼进角落，后者缩起身子、不再出声。

branches.en: THE THREAT: fear is installed on purpose so that the other person gives way.
branches.cn: 威胁线：恐惧被刻意植入，目的是让对方让步。

branches.en: THE SETTING: a cold room, a grand hall or a huge task can create the same timidity with no threat at all.
branches.cn: 场面线：冷漠的房间、宏大的厅堂或巨大的任务，不用威胁也能造出同样的胆怯。

branches.en: THE TACTIC: force is shown not to hurt but to deter, so the fear is aimed.
branches.cn: 策略线：亮出武力不是为了伤害，而是为了让人不敢动，恐惧是被瞄准的。

branches.en: THE COURT: when threats force a will, law names the act itself as an offence.
branches.cn: 法庭线：威胁一旦迫使他人意志，法律就把这一行为本身定为罪。

branches.en: THE OLD SHADE: in earlier usage the verb could simply mean to be frightening, with no victim forced to act.
branches.cn: 古旧线：早期用法中这个动词只表示本身骇人，并不一定逼迫某人行动。

intro.en: Intimidate is a built verb: a Latin fear stem, a verb ending, and English suffixes that turn it into a noun, an adjective or a person.
intro.cn: intimidate 是拼装而成的动词：拉丁语「恐惧」词干、动词词尾，再加上英语后缀，派生出名词、形容词或表示人的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin timor, timidus and medieval Latin intimidare are recorded; only the deeper origin of the fear root is source uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 timor、timidus 与中世纪拉丁语 intimidare 均有文献记录；只有更早的「恐惧」词根来源不确定。

items.example: The stem gives the whole family its sense of fear.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干赋予整个词族「恐惧」的含义。

items.example: The adjective supplies the base for the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词为动词提供基础。

items.example: The Latin verb already carried the force of the modern word.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词已带有现代词的力量。

items.example: The suffix turns the fear into an action performed on someone.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「恐惧」变成施加于人的动作。

items.meaningCN: 动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It forms intimidation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intimidation。

items.example: It forms intimidating.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intimidating。

items.example: It forms intimidator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intimidator。

items.meaning: serving to, of the nature of
items.example: It forms intimidatory, common in legal writing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intimidatory，常见于法律文本。

items.meaningCN: （由过去分词转化）表示已处于某种感受中
items.example: It forms intimidated, as in an intimidated witness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intimidated，例如「被吓住的证人」。

latinEntries.example: The noun is the base of the fear family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个名词是「恐惧」词族的基础。

latinEntries.example: Timidus survives in English as timid.
latinEntries.exampleCN: timidus 在英语中作为 timid 保留下来。

latinEntries.example: The verb sits behind the whole fear group.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个「恐惧」词组的根基。

latinEntries.example: The compound is the immediate Latin source.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个复合词是直接的拉丁语来源。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「恐吓；威胁」
由本词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「令人胆怯的；令人望而生畏的」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「被吓住的；感到胆怯的」
由本词加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「恐吓者」
由本词加形容词后缀 -atory 构成，义为「带恐吓性质的」，多用于法律语境

definition_zh: 语调；声调；吟唱；起唱音高
definition_en: the pattern of rises and falls in a voice as it speaks, carrying meaning beyond the words themselves
core_image: 一条随声音上下起伏的曲线，在句尾向上或向下拐一个弯
scene: 同一个人把同一句话说两遍，听起来却完全不像同一回事。A rising intonation turned the statement into a question.
sceneCN: 这里 intonation 是「语调」（第 1 个义项：说话时声音升降形成的起伏模式）；句意为语调上扬让一句陈述句变成了问句。图中可辨识物件：上半句上扬的曲线、下半句下落的曲线、一个问号。

pos.zh: 名词：语调；声调；吟诵；起唱音高

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词词尾回溯而成，义为「吟诵；以平缓的调子说」
由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「语调的」
由前缀 mono-（单一）加 tone（音调）构成，义为「单调的语调」
由 tone 加名词后缀 -ality 构成，义为「调性；（音乐）调体系」

senses.title: The rise and fall of a speaking voice
senses.definition: the pattern of rises and falls in pitch with which a voice speaks a phrase
senses.definitionCN: 说话时一个短语内音高上下起伏的模式
senses.example: Her calm intonation made the bad news easier to hear.
senses.exampleCN: 她平缓的语调让坏消息没那么难以接受。
senses.why: The Latin verb is built on tone, and the prefix means in or into, so intonation is the tone carried in the voice itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词由 tone（音调）与表示「在内、进入」的前缀构成，所以语调就是承载在声音里的音调。

senses.title: Pitch contrasts used instead of words
senses.titleCN: 语法层面的语调；以升降别义
senses.definition: the use of rising or falling pitch to mark a question, a statement, or a particular attitude
senses.definitionCN: 用音高升降来标明疑问、陈述或某种态度
senses.example: In English, rising intonation at the end signals that a question is coming.
senses.exampleCN: 在英语里，句尾语调整体上扬就表示要提问。
senses.why: Because the melody of a sentence can carry grammar, a rise in pitch alone turns a statement into a question.
senses.whyCN: 句子的旋律能够承担语法功能，所以单是音高上扬就能把陈述变成疑问。

senses.title: A regional or social accent melody
senses.definition: the characteristic melody of a language, region, or social group, heard even when the words are identical
senses.definitionCN: 某一语言、地区或社会群体特有的声音旋律，即使字句相同也能听出来
senses.example: The pleasant intonation of the north made every stranger sound like a friend.
senses.exampleCN: 北方那种悦耳的调子让每个陌生人都像熟人。
senses.why: Each community sings its phrases in its own way, so a shared melody becomes a badge of where a speaker comes from.
senses.whyCN: 每个群体都用各自的方式把句子唱出来，共享的旋律就成了说话人出处的标记。

senses.title: Chanting, as in prayer or recitation
senses.definition: the act of singing or reciting words on a few sustained tones, especially in worship or ritual
senses.definitionCN: 用少数持续音高把词唱出或诵出，常见于礼拜与仪式
senses.example: The monk began the slow intonation of the psalm.
senses.exampleCN: 修士开始缓缓吟诵圣咏。
senses.why: The word first names the act of making tones, and the oldest such act is singing words on a slow, steady pitch.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指「发出音调」这个动作，而最古老的此类动作就是用缓慢平稳的音高把词唱出来。

senses.title: Accuracy of pitch in music
senses.definition: the exactness of a sung or played pitch, or the starting pitch given before singing
senses.definitionCN: 演唱或演奏时音高的准确程度，或开唱前给出的起始音
senses.example: The choir sang with good intonation but uncertain rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 合唱团音准不错，节奏却不够稳。
senses.why: Once it was used for chants in church, the same word was borrowed for any concern about being on the right pitch.
senses.whyCN: 一旦用于教堂吟唱，这个词自然被借去指任何「音高是否正确」的问题。

intro.en: Intonation is the Latin verb intonare made into a noun: a tone is put inside the voice, and that carried tone becomes the pattern we hear.
intro.cn: intonation 由拉丁语动词 intonare 变来名词：把音调放进声音里，这个被承载的音调就成了我们听到的起伏。

items.en: In medieval Latin, intonare is formed from in plus tonare, to thunder, and comes to mean to sing or strike up a tune.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中，intonare 由 in 与 tonare（打雷）构成，意为「起调、唱起来」。

items.en: Behind tonare stands the noun tonus, borrowed from Greek, which means a stretching and later a pitch or tone.
items.cn: tonare 背后是名词 tonus，借自希腊语，本义为「拉紧」，后来指音高、音调。

items.en: French forms the noun intonation, naming the way a chant is begun and sustained.
items.cn: 法语构成名词 intonation，指吟唱开始与延续的方式。

items.en: English borrows intonation in the seventeenth century, first for the chanting of psalms in church.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入 intonation，最初指教堂中吟唱诗篇。

items.en: The noun moves from church chant to ordinary speech, to the melody of regional accents, then to singing in tune.
items.cn: 这个词从教堂吟唱转到日常说话，再到地域口音的旋律，最后指唱歌音准。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin tone root and its English offshoots; the near-meaning group gathers other names for how a voice or a line of music moves.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「音调」词根及其英语派生词；近义组收其他描述声音或旋律走向的说法。

entries.definition: To speak or sing in a slow, steady voice; the verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吟诵、以平缓的调子说」，是本词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The quality or pitch of a sound, and in language the pitch meaning of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「音调、音色」，在语言中也可指一个词的字调。

entries.definition: Relating to intonation; a technical adjective of linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「语调的」，是语言学术语。

entries.definition: A single unvarying tone, used for a voice that never rises or falls.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「单调的语调」，指始终不升不降的声音。

entries.definition: The general attitude carried by a voice or a text; wider and less technical than intonation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「语气、色调」，泛指声音或文字带出的态度，比本词宽泛。

entries.definition: How high or low a single sound is; intonation is the pattern built from many pitches.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「音高」，指单个声音的高低；语调由许多音高组成。

entries.definition: The extra emphasis given to a syllable, heard in loudness rather than in pitch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「重音」，指对音节的额外强调，靠响度而非音高。

entries.definition: The way a group pronounces sounds and places stress; intonation is only its melody.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「口音」，指一群人发音与重音的方式；语调只是其中的旋律部分。

entries.definition: The changing of pitch in speech, especially as it shows feeling; close to intonation but narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（说话）抑扬」，多用来体现情感，接近本词但范围更窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin tone root and the collocations the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子依据真实的拉丁语「音调」词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: The heart of the word is tone: intonation is the tone carried through a whole phrase.
normal.cn: 这个词的核心是 tone：语调是贯穿整个短语的音调。

normal.en: The prefix means in, so the tone is put inside the voice rather than written above it.
normal.cn: 前缀表示「进入」，音调是被放进声音里的，而不是写在纸上。

normal.en: Rising intonation usually ends a question; falling intonation usually ends a statement.
normal.cn: 升调通常结束一个问句；降调通常结束一个陈述句。

normal.en: The verb intone means to chant slowly, and the noun grew straight out of that chanting.
normal.cn: 动词 intone 意为缓慢吟诵，名词正是从这种吟唱中长出来的。

normal.en: Compare tone and intonation: tone is one shade, intonation is the whole moving line.
normal.cn: 对比 tone 与 intonation：tone 是单块颜色，intonation 是整条游走的曲线。

abstract.en: Picture the same sentence drawn twice, once as a hill that climbs at the end, once as a slope that falls.
abstract.cn: 想象把同一句话画两遍：一处是末尾向上爬的山坡，一处是往下落的斜坡。

abstract.en: A flat line sounds bored, a high arch sounds surprised: the shape of the line is part of the message.
abstract.cn: 平直的线听起来无聊，高拱的线听起来惊讶：线条的形状本身就是信息的一部分。

abstract.en: A single church chant and a whole conversation share the same curve: the voice keeps drawing the same hills.
abstract.cn: 一段教堂吟唱和一场日常对话共享同一种曲线：声音始终在画同样的山丘。

examples.en: Teachers corrected the students not only on sounds but also on intonation.
examples.cn: 老师不仅纠正学生的发音，也纠正他们的语调。

examples.en: Listen to the intonation of the speaker and guess her mood.
examples.cn: 听一听说话人的语调，猜猜她的心情。

examples.en: The choir worked for hours on intonation before the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会前，合唱团花了好几个小时练习音准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「音通内伸」——声音一进一出、一高一低，像线一样伸进去；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 intonare 由 in（进入）与 tonare（打雷）构成，tonare 又出自借自希腊语的 tonus（拉紧；音调）。法语据此构成名词 intonation，十七世纪进入英语，最初指吟唱诗篇。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses keep the same inner tone: the rise and fall of a speaking voice, pitch used as grammar, the melody of an accent, chanting, and being in tune.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项都保留同一个「内在音调」：说话声音的升降、用作语法的音高、口音的旋律、吟唱，以及音准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of notes rises and dips with the voice, and at the end of the sentence it turns up or down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串音符随着声音升高低落，在句尾向上或向下拐一个弯。

branches.en: THE VOICE: the everyday sense is simply the pitch pattern inside a spoken phrase.
branches.cn: 声音线：最日常的义项就是一句话里音高的起伏模式。

branches.en: THE GRAMMAR: the shape of the line can carry a question or an attitude without any extra word.
branches.cn: 语法线：线条的形状本身能带上疑问或态度，不需要额外的词。

branches.en: THE ACCENT: a community draws the same hills, so its melody becomes a mark of origin.
branches.cn: 口音线：一个群体画着同样的山丘，旋律就成了出身的标记。

branches.en: THE CHANT: the oldest sense is the slow reciting of words on a few held tones.
branches.cn: 吟诵线：最古老的义项是用少数持续音高缓缓诵词。

branches.en: THE TUNING: church chant led to the musical sense of being exactly on pitch.
branches.cn: 音准线：教堂吟唱引出音乐中「音高是否准确」的义项。

intro.en: Intonation is built on the Latin root for sound and tone, with an in- prefix and an English -ion ending.
intro.cn: intonation 建立在拉丁语「声音、音调」词根上，由 in- 前缀与英语后缀 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin tonus is borrowed from Greek tonos, meaning a stretching and then a pitch; tonare means to thunder.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tonus 借自希腊语 tonos，本义「拉紧」，后指音调；tonare 意为「打雷」。

items.example: The prefix puts the tone inside the voice.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把音调放进声音里。

items.example: The verb supplies the sound-making stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「发声」的词干。

items.example: The noun gives the family its sense of pitch.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词赋予词族「音高」的含义。

items.meaning: to sing, to strike up a tune
items.example: The Latin verb joins the prefix and the sounding verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词把前缀与「发声」动词合在一起。

items.meaningCN: 动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the noun intonation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变为名词 intonation。

items.example: It forms intonational, used in phonetics.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 intonational，用于语音学。

items.meaning: pitch or quality of a sound
items.example: Tone is the short English relative of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: tone 是整个词族在英语中的简短亲缘词。

items.example: With tone it forms monotone.
items.exampleCN: 与 tone 结合构成 monotone。

items.meaning: the key or tonal system of a piece of music
items.example: Tonality is another modern relative built on the tone root.
items.exampleCN: tonality 是建立在「音调」词根上的另一个现代亲属词。

latinEntries.example: Tonus is the source of tone and intonation alike.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tonus 是 tone 与 intonation 的共同来源。

latinEntries.example: The verb of loud sound feeds intonare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个表示巨响的动词为 intonare 提供词干。

latinEntries.meaning: to sing, strike up a tune
latinEntries.example: Intonare is the immediate Latin source.
latinEntries.exampleCN: intonare 是直接的拉丁语来源。

latinEntries.example: The Latin noun already named the starting of a chant.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已指吟唱的开始。

definition_zh: 使醉酒；使中毒；使陶醉；使极度兴奋
definition_en: to make someone drunk, poisoned, or wildly excited, as if their self-control had been taken away
core_image: 一杯掺了毒物的酒被人一饮而尽，酒入喉咙后连脑子一起被搅乱
scene: 宴席上有人贪杯，起初只是话多，后来站起来就摇摇晃晃。One guest drank far too much at the banquet and was soon quite intoxicated.
sceneCN: 这里 intoxicate 是「使醉酒」（第 1 个义项：饮酒过量而醉）；句意：一位客人在宴席上喝得太多，很快就醉得不轻。

pos.zh: 使醉；使中毒；使陶醉；使极度兴奋

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「醉酒；中毒；陶醉」
由动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「令人陶醉的；醉人的」
由动词加表示「物」的后缀构成，义为「致醉物质；酒类」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「醉的；陶醉的；极度兴奋的」

senses.title: To make someone drunk
senses.definition: to make a person drunk through alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 用酒精使人醉倒
senses.example: Three glasses of wine were enough to intoxicate him.
senses.exampleCN: 三杯葡萄酒就足以让他醉倒。
senses.why: Alcohol behaves like poison in the body, so the Latin idea of a toxin inside the drink quietly became the everyday idea of being drunk.
senses.whyCN: 酒精在体内像毒物一样起作用，于是拉丁语中「酒里含毒」的想法悄然转成了日常的「醉酒」。

senses.title: To poison with a substance
senses.definition: to harm a person or animal with a toxin or poisoned substance
senses.definitionCN: 用毒物伤害人或动物
senses.example: Certain plants intoxicate grazing animals without killing them.
senses.exampleCN: 有些植物会让吃草的牲畜中毒，但并不致命。
senses.why: The Latin noun toxicum meant a poison for arrows, and intoxicate keeps that medical and chemical sense today.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 toxicum 本指涂在箭上的毒，intoxicate 至今保留着这个医学与化学义。

senses.title: To fill with wild excitement
senses.definition: to fill a person with such strong feeling that their judgement suffers
senses.definitionCN: 用强烈的情感充满一个人，以致判断力受损
senses.example: Early victories seemed to intoxicate the young captain.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的胜利似乎让那位年轻上尉忘乎所以。
senses.why: If a drink can blind a person, so can success or love, so the physical drunk grew into an emotional one.
senses.whyCN: 酒能让人看不清，成功或爱情也能，于是身体上的醉酒延伸为情感上的陶醉。

senses.title: Intoxicating in smell or taste
senses.definition: strong and sweet in a way that pleases the senses almost too much
senses.definitionCN: 气味或味道浓烈甜美到几乎让人招架不住
senses.example: The garden was full of intoxicating scents at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时整座花园弥漫着醉人的香气。
senses.why: Smell and taste act on the body directly, so the word is applied to fragrances and flavours that work like a strong drink.
senses.whyCN: 气味与味道直接作用于身体，所以这个词也被用于像烈酒一样起作用的香气与风味。

intro.en: Intoxicate comes from Medieval Latin intoxicare, to poison, built from in-, into, and toxicum, a poison for arrows.
intro.cn: intoxicate 来自中世纪拉丁语 intoxicare（使中毒），由 in-（进入）与 toxicum（箭毒）构成。

items.en: Toxikon meant a bow, from toxon, and arrow poison was named after the weapon.
items.cn: 希腊语 toxikon 本指射箭之物，源自 toxon（弓），箭毒便以武器命名。

items.en: Toxicum names a poison for tipping arrows.
items.cn: 拉丁语 toxicum 指涂在箭头上的毒。

items.en: Intoxicare adds in-, into, and means to poison or to drug.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 intoxicare 加上 in-（进入），意为使中毒、下药。

items.en: The verb enters English in medical writing with the sense of poisoning.
items.cn: 这个动词在医学文献中进入英语，先取「使中毒」义。

items.en: Drunkenness becomes the main everyday sense.
items.cn: 醉酒成为日常最主要的义项。

items.en: Figurative uses with success, power, and scent are common.
items.cn: 现代英语中，成功、权力、香气等隐喻用法十分常见。

note.en: Intoxicate belongs to the toxicum family of medical words and stands beside drunk, exhilarate, and the everyday phrase tipsy.
note.cn: intoxicate 属于 toxicum（毒）这一医学词族，并与 drunk、exhilarate 以及口语 tipsy 相邻。

entries.definition: poisonous
entries.definitionCN: 有毒的

entries.definition: a poison produced by a living thing
entries.definitionCN: 毒素

entries.definition: the state of being drunk or poisoned
entries.definitionCN: 醉酒；中毒

entries.definition: a period of removing harmful substances
entries.definitionCN: 解毒；排毒

entries.definition: having drunk too much alcohol
entries.definitionCN: 醉的

entries.definition: to give a harmful substance to a person or animal
entries.definitionCN: 毒害；下毒

entries.definition: to make someone feel very happy and lively
entries.definitionCN: 使兴奋；使振奋

normalIntro.en: Intoxicate keeps the Latin word for arrow poison hidden inside it.
normalIntro.cn: intoxicate 里藏着拉丁语「箭毒」这个词。

normal.en: Intoxicate is the verb, intoxication the noun, and intoxicated the adjective.
normal.cn: intoxicate 是动词，intoxication 是名词，intoxicated 是形容词。

normal.en: The prefix in- means into, so intoxicate is to put poison into a person.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 表示「进入」，所以 intoxicate 是把毒放进一个人身体里。

normal.en: Be intoxicated by success means success has gone to your head.
normal.cn: be intoxicated by success 意为被成功冲昏了头脑。

normal.en: An intoxicating smell is so strong and sweet that it almost makes you dizzy.
normal.cn: intoxicating smell 指浓烈甜美的气味，几乎让人发晕。

normal.en: Compare excited: intoxicated suggests a loss of control that excited does not.
normal.cn: 对比 excited：intoxicated 含有失控的意味，而 excited 没有。

abstract.en: Picture a wine glass with a dark drop of poison at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只酒杯，杯底有一滴黑色的毒。

abstract.en: Imagine a hunter dipping an arrow into a bitter liquid.
abstract.cn: 想象猎手把箭浸入苦涩的药液。

abstract.en: Think of a young officer whose head spins after a victory medal.
abstract.cn: 想象一位年轻军官戴上胜利勋章后头脑发晕。

examples.en: The doctor warned that the fumes could intoxicate workers in the tunnel.
examples.cn: 医生警告说，那些气体可能使隧道里的工人中毒。

examples.en: Success did not intoxicate the quiet engineer.
examples.cn: 成功并没有让那位安静的工程师忘乎所以。

examples.en: The bakery sends out an intoxicating smell of butter.
examples.cn: 面包店飘出醉人的黄油香气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因它死气开特」——喝了它，人就「死气」沉沉地开挂了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关，真正的词根是「毒」。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ toxicum（箭毒，源自希腊语 toxikon，与 toxon「弓」相关）→ 中世纪拉丁语 intoxicare（使中毒）→ 英语 intoxicate，核心义「把毒灌进身体」。

sensesIntro.en: Intoxicate begins with poison from a drink, narrows to drunkenness, and then stretches to any excitement that takes away control.
sensesIntro.cn: intoxicate 从饮品中的毒说起，收窄为醉酒，再伸向任何让人失去控制的兴奋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a poisoned drink going down a thirsty throat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杯有毒的酒灌进干渴的喉咙。

branches.en: Alcohol is the poison that modern speakers mean first.
branches.cn: 酒精是现代人最先想到的那种「毒」。

branches.en: The original medical sense of poisoning survives in scientific writing.
branches.cn: 原始的「使中毒」医学义在科学写作中保留下来。

branches.en: Success or love can act like a drink and blind the mind.
branches.cn: 成功或爱情可以像酒一样蒙住心智。

branches.en: Wine and perfume both reach the senses and bend them.
branches.cn: 酒与香水都直接触及感官，并让其倾斜。

branches.en: A toxin and a strong feeling both take away a persons control.
branches.cn: 毒物与强烈情感都会夺走一个人的自控力。

intro.en: Intoxicate is built from the prefix in- and the Latin poison word toxicum, with a whole family of toxic words around it.
intro.cn: intoxicate 由前缀 in- 与拉丁语词「毒」toxicum 构成，周围是一整族 toxic 词。

latinIntro.en: Latin toxicum means a poison for arrows, and intoxicare means to poison.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 toxicum 意为箭毒，intoxicare 意为使中毒。

items.example: The prefix in- means into, as in intoxicare.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 表示「进入」，如 intoxicare 中的用法。

items.example: Toxicum is the poison word inside intoxicate.
items.exampleCN: toxicum 是藏在 intoxicate 里的「毒」。

items.example: Intoxicare is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: intoxicare 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: Intoxicate keeps both the poison and the drunk sense.
items.exampleCN: intoxicate 同时保留「中毒」与「醉酒」两个含义。

items.example: The suffix -ate turns the Latin stem into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 把这个拉丁语词干变成动词。

items.meaningCN: 状态或动作的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms intoxication.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 intoxication。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms intoxicant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成 intoxicant。

items.meaningCN: 具有某性质的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms intoxicating.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 intoxicating。

items.example: Toxic keeps the bare poison stem.
items.exampleCN: toxic 保留了裸露的「毒」词干。

items.example: Detox uses de- to take the poison away.
items.exampleCN: detox 用 de- 表示把毒拿掉。

definition_zh: 无畏的；勇敢的；无所畏惧的
definition_en: very brave and showing no fear in dangerous or difficult situations
core_image: 一位探险者脚下是结冰的裂谷，他没有回头看，只是继续向前迈步
scene: 风暴把帆扯成两半，多数船员退回舱内，只有那位老船长还站在船头。Even after the storm tore the sails, the old captain stayed at the bow, calm and intrepid.
sceneCN: 这里 intrepid 是「无畏的」（第 1 个义项：面对危险毫无畏惧）；句意：即便风暴撕破了帆，老船长仍留在船头，镇定而无畏。

pos.zh: 无畏的；勇敢的；无所畏惧的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词词尾 -ly 构成，义为「无畏地」
由形容词加名词词尾 -ity 构成，义为「无畏；勇敢」
去掉否定前缀 in- 后的同源词，义为「惶恐；不安」

senses.title: Fearless in the face of danger
senses.definition: showing no fear when real danger is present
senses.definitionCN: 在真正的危险面前毫不畏惧
senses.example: An intrepid climber rescued the stranded hikers.
senses.exampleCN: 一位无畏的登山者救下了受困的徒步者。
senses.why: The Latin word means not trembling, so the image is a person whose hands stay steady while everything around shakes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在拉丁语中意为「不发抖」，画面是一个人在周围一切摇晃时双手依然稳当。

senses.title: Bold in a difficult task
senses.definition: bold and determined when a task is hard, unpleasant, or unpopular
senses.definitionCN: 在任务艰难、不愉快或不受欢迎时果断而勇敢
senses.example: The intrepid team kept writing despite the threats.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管受到威胁，这支敢闯的团队仍坚持写作。
senses.why: Fear is not only felt in physical risk, so the same steadiness is applied to hard work that frightens most people.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧不只来自身体上的危险，所以同一份镇定也被用在让大多数人害怕的艰难工作上。

senses.title: Adventurous and eager for the unknown
senses.definition: having a lively taste for adventure and unfamiliar places
senses.definitionCN: 对冒险与陌生地方怀有热烈兴趣
senses.example: Intrepid readers love tales of faraway seas.
senses.exampleCN: 爱冒险的读者喜欢遥远海域的故事。
senses.why: People who do not tremble enjoy the unknown instead of avoiding it, so the word also carries a cheerful taste for adventure.
senses.whyCN: 不发抖的人会把未知当成乐趣而不是躲开，于是这个词也带上了对冒险的欢快兴趣。

senses.title: Used in a slightly ironic tone
senses.definition: used humorously about someone who is too confident about something small
senses.definitionCN: 幽默地形容对小事过于自信的人
senses.example: Only the intrepid staff dared to ask for a second biscuit.
senses.exampleCN: 只有那些「勇猛」的员工才敢再要一块饼干。
senses.why: A grand word placed next to a small matter turns into a gentle joke, so the high literary tone becomes an ironic one.
senses.whyCN: 把一个大词放在小事旁边就变成了温和的笑话，于是高雅的文学腔调转成了反讽。

intro.en: Intrepid comes from French intrépide, from Latin intrepidus, not trembling, built from in-, not, and trepidus, alarmed or shaking.
intro.cn: intrepid 来自法语 intrépide，源于拉丁语 intrepidus（不发抖），由 in-（不）与 trepidus（惊慌、发抖）构成。

items.en: Trepidus means alarmed, hurried, or shaking with fear.
items.cn: 拉丁语 trepidus 意为惊慌的、匆忙的、因恐惧而发抖的。

items.en: Intrepidus puts the negative prefix in- in front and means not trembling.
items.cn: intrepidus 在前面加上否定前缀 in-，意为不发抖。

items.en: Intrépide carries the word into French, still literary in tone.
items.cn: 法语 intrépide 把这个词带过去，语气依然偏文学。

items.en: Intrepid enters English in the sense of fearless.
items.cn: intrepid 在英语中进入使用，义为无畏的。

items.en: The word settles in travel writing about explorers and reporters.
items.cn: 在现代英语里，这个词常用于描写探险家与记者的游记报道。

note.en: Intrepid belongs to the trepidus family, with trepidation and trepid on one side and brave, fearless, and audacious on the other.
note.cn: intrepid 属于 trepidus（发抖）词族，一边是 trepidation 与 trepid，另一边是 brave、fearless 与 audacious。

entries.definitionCN: 惶恐；不安

entries.definition: great courage

entries.definition: willing to face danger

entries.definition: showing no fear at all

entries.definition: confident and ready to take risks
