normalIntro.en: Intrepid is a negative word about trembling, so it literally says no shaking.
normalIntro.cn: intrepid 是一个关于「发抖」的否定词，字面意思是「不发抖」。

normal.en: The prefix in- means not, and trepidus means trembling.
normal.cn: 前缀 in- 表示「不」，trepidus 表示发抖。

normal.en: Trepidation is the fear, and intrepid is the person without it.
normal.cn: trepidation 是恐惧，intrepid 则是没有这种恐惧的人。

normal.en: An intrepid explorer is the writer favourite for wild places.
normal.cn: intrepid explorer 是写荒野时作者最爱的说法。

normal.en: Intrepid is more literary than brave, so it suits stories and reports.
normal.cn: intrepid 比 brave 更文学化，适合故事与报道。

normal.en: Keep the spelling straight: intrepid, not intreppid or interpid.
normal.cn: 拼写要记牢：是 intrepid，不要写成 intreppid 或 interpid。

abstract.en: Picture a climber on a cracked glacier whose tent rope has just snapped.
abstract.cn: 想象一位登山者站在开裂的冰川上，帐篷绳刚刚断开。

abstract.en: Imagine a reporter walking into a crowd where no one else will go.
abstract.cn: 想象一位记者走进别人都不敢去的群集之中。

abstract.en: Think of a child who rows a small boat towards a hidden island.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子划着小船驶向一座隐蔽的小岛。

examples.en: The intrepid sailors crossed the ocean on a wooden boat.
examples.cn: 无畏的水手们靠一条木船横渡了大洋。

examples.en: She wrote an intrepid account of life inside the prison.
examples.cn: 她写下了一份关于狱中生活的无所畏惧的记录。

examples.en: Few intrepid volunteers agreed to enter the collapsing house.
examples.cn: 很少有勇敢的志愿者愿意进入那栋正在倒塌的房屋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因吹皮得」——因为他吹了牛还把皮披得紧紧的，才敢往前闯；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关，真正的词根是「不发抖」。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ trepidus（发抖、惊慌）→ intrepidus（不发抖的）→ 法语 intrépide → 英语 intrepid，核心义「腿不发抖」。

sensesIntro.en: Intrepid starts from a body that does not shake, then widens to bold work, to a love of adventure, and finally to a mild joke.
sensesIntro.cn: intrepid 从「身体不发抖」出发，扩展到大胆的工作、对冒险的热爱，最后还带上一点玩笑意味。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steady hand on a rope while the cliff shakes.
core.cn: 核心意象：崖壁在晃，握住绳索的手却稳稳不动。

branches.en: No fear in real danger is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 在真正的危险前毫无畏惧是字面义项。

branches.en: No fear at hard work is the everyday extension.
branches.cn: 面对艰难工作不退缩是日常的延伸义。

branches.en: A taste for the unknown is the cheerful side.
branches.cn: 对未知的喜爱是这个词欢快的一面。

branches.en: Explorers show both physical courage and a love of the road.
branches.cn: 探险家同时表现出身体上的勇气与对远路的喜爱。

branches.en: The same word can describe a hero and gently mock a clerk.
branches.cn: 同一个词既能形容英雄，也能轻轻调侃一位职员。

intro.en: Intrepid is a Latin negative prefix in- on the stem trepid, with trepidation and the adverb intrepidly as close relatives.
intro.cn: intrepid 是拉丁语否定前缀 in- 加上词干 trepid，近亲是 trepidation 与副词 intrepidly。

latinIntro.en: Latin trepidus means alarmed or shaking, and intrepidus means not shaking.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trepidus 意为惊慌、发抖，intrepidus 意为不发抖。

items.example: The prefix in- gives the word its negative sense.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 给这个词带来否定意味。

items.example: Trepidus supplies the trembling image.
items.exampleCN: trepidus 提供「发抖」的意象。

items.example: Intrepidus is the direct source form.
items.exampleCN: intrepidus 是直接来源形式。

items.example: Intrepid keeps the full Latin shape.
items.exampleCN: intrepid 保留了完整的拉丁语形体。

items.meaningCN: 以某种方式的副词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms intrepidly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 intrepidly。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms intrepidity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 intrepidity。

items.meaningCN: 状态或动作的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms trepidation.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 trepidation。

items.example: Trepidation is intrepid with the negative prefix dropped.
items.exampleCN: trepidation 就是去掉否定前缀的 intrepid 同源词。

items.example: Trepid is the rare bare form of the stem.
items.exampleCN: trepid 是这个词干罕见的裸露形式。

items.example: Intrepidly describes the manner of an action.
items.exampleCN: intrepidly 描述动作的方式。

definition_zh: 激起好奇心；使着迷；密谋；阴谋；私通
definition_en: to make someone very curious or fascinated, or to plot secretly against others
core_image: 几个人在烛光下凑近低声交谈，桌上摊着一张写满暗号的纸
scene: 新的展览海报只露出半张画，看的人总想再往下翻。The half hidden exhibit poster intrigued every visitor who passed.
sceneCN: 这里 intrigue 是「激起好奇心」（第 1 个义项：使人非常好奇）；句意：那张只露出一半的展览海报让每个路过的访客都心生好奇。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加形容词词尾构成，义为「引人入胜的；有趣的」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「好奇的；被勾起了兴趣的」
由动词加表示「人」的词尾构成，义为「密谋者；耍阴谋的人」
由同源形容词 intricate 加名词词尾构成，义为「错综复杂」

senses.title: To make someone very curious
senses.definition: to make a person want to know more about something mysterious
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人想更多了解某件神秘的事
senses.example: The stranger story intrigued the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 那个陌生人的故事勾起了整个村子的好奇。
senses.why: Something tangled is hard to leave alone, so a puzzle that entangles the mind makes people want to keep looking.
senses.whyCN: 纠缠在一起的东西让人忍不住想弄明白，于是缠住心思的谜题就让人想一直看下去。

senses.title: To fascinate and attract
senses.definition: to hold a persons attention strongly and pleasantly
senses.definitionCN: 强烈而愉快地抓住一个人的注意力
senses.example: Her quiet voice intrigued the audience at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她安静的声音立刻让听众着迷。
senses.why: Curiosity that grows into charm keeps a person in place, so intrigue also means a strong pull towards someone or something.
senses.whyCN: 好奇心一旦长成魅力就让人挪不开步子，所以 intrigue 也指对某人某物的强烈吸引。

senses.title: To plot in secret
senses.definition: to plan something secret and dishonest with other people
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起策划隐秘而不正当的事情
senses.example: Two ministers intrigued against the king.
senses.exampleCN: 两位大臣密谋反对国王。
senses.why: A plot is a maze of private meetings, so the tangled Latin sense survives as the verb for plotting.
senses.whyCN: 阴谋就是一堆私下的会面绕成迷宫，所以拉丁语中「缠结」的意味保存为「密谋」这个动词义。

senses.title: A secret plan
senses.definition: a secret plan made by several people against others
senses.definitionCN: 几个人针对他人制定的秘密计划
senses.example: The election was full of political intrigue.
senses.exampleCN: 那场选举中充满了政治阴谋。
senses.why: The verb became a noun, naming the whole knotted affair rather than one action.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词转成名词，指的不再是一个动作，而是整团纠缠不清的事件。

senses.title: A secret love affair
senses.definition: a secret romantic relationship, especially in older or literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 秘密的恋情，多见于较旧或文学性的写作
senses.example: The novel is full of court intrigue and hidden letters.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说里满是宫廷私情与藏起来的信件。
senses.why: Secret meetings are the same material as plotting, so intrigue grew a third branch about hidden love.
senses.whyCN: 秘密会面与阴谋用的是同样的材料，于是 intrigue 又长出了关于隐秘恋情的第三个分支。

intro.en: Intrigue comes from French intriguer, from Italian intrigo and intrigare, and behind them Latin intricare, to entangle.
intro.cn: intrigue 来自法语 intriguer，源于意大利语 intrigo 与 intrigare，再往前是拉丁语 intricare（使缠结）。

items.en: Intricare means to entangle or to put something in the way.
items.cn: 拉丁语 intricare 意为使缠结、设置障碍。

items.en: Intrigare means to scheme, and intrigo names a plot.
items.cn: 意大利语 intrigare 意为暗地里谋划，intrigo 指阴谋。

items.en: Intriguer carries both the plotting and the secret love sense.
items.cn: 法语 intriguer 同时携带「密谋」与「秘密恋情」两义。

items.en: Intrigue enters English as a noun of court and political plotting.
items.cn: intrigue 作为宫廷与政治密谋的名词进入英语。

items.en: The verb extends to mean to arouse curiosity.
items.cn: 动词义扩展到「引起好奇心」。

note.en: Intrigue sits in the intricare tangle family, and its everyday charm sense stands beside fascinate and intrigued.
note.cn: intrigue 属于 intricare（缠结）词族，日常的「迷人」义则与 fascinate 以及 intrigued 相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 使摆脱困境

entries.definitionCN: 扳机；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to interest someone very strongly
entries.definitionCN: 使着迷；使极感兴趣

entries.definition: a secret plan by a group to do wrong
entries.definitionCN: 阴谋；密谋

entries.definition: a secret plan, often dishonest
entries.definitionCN: 计划；狡计

normalIntro.en: Intrigue is a two faced word: one face is charm, the other face is plotting.
normalIntro.cn: intrigue 是一张两面词：一面是吸引，另一面是勾心斗角。

normal.en: The Latin source intricare means to entangle, and intricate is its adjective cousin.
normal.cn: 它的拉丁来源 intricare 意为「使缠结」，intricate 就是它的形容词表亲。

normal.en: Be intrigued by something means curiosity has been caught.
normal.cn: be intrigued by 某物表示好奇心被抓住了。

normal.en: Political intrigue names the tangled game of power.
normal.cn: political intrigue 指权力场上缠成一团的博弈。

normal.en: An intriguing idea is one you cannot stop thinking about.
normal.cn: intriguing idea 指让你停不下来去想的想法。

normal.en: The noun keeps a page of a novel: intrigue, secrets, hidden letters.
normal.cn: 这个名词常和小说的一页连在一起：阴谋、秘密、藏起来的信。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed letter with a crooked wax mark on the front.
abstract.cn: 想象一封封口的信，封蜡上按着一个歪斜的印记。

abstract.en: Imagine a magnet quietly pulling iron dust across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一块磁铁在桌面悄悄把铁屑吸过来。

abstract.en: Think of two men whispering behind a heavy red curtain.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人在厚重的红幕布后面低声交谈。

examples.en: The odd symbol on the map intrigued the young historian.
examples.cn: 地图上那个古怪的符号让年轻的历史学家很感兴趣。

examples.en: Years of court intrigue made the palace dangerous.
examples.cn: 多年的宫廷阴谋让这座宫殿变得危险。

examples.en: Some colleagues intrigued against the new director.
examples.cn: 有些同事密谋反对新来的主管。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因缺个」——因为缺一个证据，所以大家更好奇、更着迷；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关，真正的核心是「缠在一起」。

root: 拉丁语 intricare（使缠结）→ 意大利语 intrigare（暗地谋划）→ 法语 intriguer → 英语 intrigue，核心义「把线缠成一团」。

sensesIntro.en: Intrigue begins with threads tangled together, splits into secret plotting and secret love, and then softens into the pull of a clever mystery.
sensesIntro.cn: intrigue 从缠在一起的线团说起，分出秘密谋划与隐秘恋情两支，最后软化为聪明谜题带来的吸引力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: threads wound into a knot that no one can untie.
core.cn: 核心意象：线绕成一个没人解得开的结。

branches.en: A knot in the mind is what makes a person curious.
branches.cn: 心里打了一个结，人就会好奇。

branches.en: Curiosity that stays becomes a strong attraction.
branches.cn: 停留下来的好奇心变成了强烈的吸引。

branches.en: Hidden meetings of plotters are the old core sense.
branches.cn: 密谋者的私下会面是这个词最老的核心义。

branches.en: The verb and the noun describe the same action from two sides.
branches.cn: 动词与名词从两个侧面描述同一个动作。

branches.en: A secret love and a hidden clue both keep people guessing.
branches.cn: 秘密恋情与隐藏线索都让人猜个不停。

intro.en: Intrigue is a Latin tangle word that reached English through Italian and French, with intricate and intriguing in its family.
intro.cn: intrigue 是一个表示「缠结」的拉丁词，经意大利语与法语进入英语，词族中有 intricate 与 intriguing。

latinIntro.en: Latin intricare means to entangle, and tricae means tricks or trouble.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intricare 意为使缠结，tricae 意为花招、麻烦。

items.example: The prefix in- gives intensification or location.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 表示加强或位置。

items.meaning: tricks, tricks of the mind, trouble
items.example: Tricae supplies the trickery that lives inside the word.
items.exampleCN: tricae 把这个词里暗藏的「狡诈」带了进来。

items.example: Intricare is the oldest known source.
items.exampleCN: intricare 是目前已知最早的来源。

items.example: Intrigare gave the plotting branch.
items.exampleCN: intrigare 提供了「密谋」这个分支。

items.example: Intrigue first named secret plots in English.
items.exampleCN: intrigue 最初在英语中指秘密的谋划。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms intriguing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 intriguing。

items.meaningCN: 处于某状态的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms intrigued.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 intrigued。

items.example: The suffix -er forms intriguer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 intriguer。

items.example: Intricate keeps the tangle in adjective form.
items.exampleCN: intricate 以形容词形式保留了「缠结」。

items.example: Extricate uses ex- to untangle the knot.
items.exampleCN: extricate 用前缀 ex- 来表达「解开结」。

definition_zh: 内省；自省；内省式自我观察
definition_en: the careful habit of looking inward to examine your own thoughts and feelings
core_image: 一个人停在原地，转身低头，往自己心里看上一眼
scene: 深夜写日记的人放下笔，先把当天那些说不出口的情绪逐条翻出来看一遍。Nightly introspection turned the vague unease in her chest into three questions she could answer.
sceneCN: 这里 introspection 是「内省、自省」（第 1 个义项：往回看自己心里的念头与感受）；句意：每夜的自省把胸口那团说不清的不安，变成了三个她能回答的问题。

pos.zh: 内省；自省；对自身思想的检视

derivatives.zh: introspection + -ive，义为「内省的；爱自省的」
由 introspection 逆构而成，义为「内省；反省」
introspective + -ly，义为「以内省的方式」

senses.title: The act of looking inward
senses.definition: the habit or act of carefully examining your own thoughts, motives, and feelings
senses.definitionCN: 认真检视自己念头、动机与感受的习惯或举动
senses.example: A quiet walk gives her time for honest introspection.
senses.exampleCN: 一段安静的散步给了她诚实地检视自己的时间。
senses.why: Latin intro means within and specere means to look, so introspection is literally a looking within, the gaze turned around onto the mind itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intro 意为「在内」，specere 意为「看」：introspection 字面上就是「往里看」，把目光转回自己的心智上。

senses.title: Introspection as a method
senses.definition: a deliberate method of studying thinking by observing and reporting your own inner experience
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察并报告自身内在体验来研究思维的一种自觉方法
senses.example: Early psychologists treated introspection as a laboratory technique.
senses.exampleCN: 早期心理学家把内省当作实验室里的一种技术。
senses.why: Once the inward look is trained and reported step by step, the private habit becomes a public method that others can repeat.
senses.whyCN: 当「往里看」被训练、被一步步报告出来，私人的习惯就变成别人也能重复的公开方法。

senses.title: Self-examination with judgment
senses.definition: a period of serious self-examination in which a person judges their own behaviour and choices
senses.definitionCN: 认真审视自身、评判自己行为与选择的时期
senses.example: The failure led to a year of painful introspection.
senses.exampleCN: 那次失败引来了长达一年的痛苦反省。
senses.why: Looking inward easily turns into looking at yourself from outside, so the mental gaze becomes an act of judging your own conduct.
senses.whyCN: 往心里看很容易变成从外面看自己，于是这束心理上的目光就带上了评判自身行为的意味。

senses.title: The literary inward turn
senses.definition: the practice in writing of turning inward to explore a character or narrator state of mind in detail
senses.definitionCN: 写作中转向内心、细致探索人物或叙述者心理的写法
senses.example: The novel is famous for its long passages of introspection.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说以大量漫长的内心描写闻名。
senses.why: The same inward gaze is a visible craft in literature, where the look into the mind is written down line by line.
senses.whyCN: 同一种向内看的目光在文学里是一种可见的手艺：对内心的观察被一行行写了下来。

senses.title: The poetic sense of vision
senses.definition: in older poetic use, the power of seeing into the inner nature of things
senses.definitionCN: 在较古老的诗歌用语中指看透事物内在性质的能力
senses.example: The poet claimed introspection into the hearts of ordinary objects.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人自称能看透寻常事物的内里。
senses.why: The intro- prefix can also mean into, so the same word was once stretched beyond the self to mean looking into the inside of anything.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 intro- 也能表示「进入」，所以这个词曾被伸展到自我之外，指看到任何事物的内部。

intro.en: Introspection joins Latin intro, within, to specere, to look, so it first meant a looking into, especially into things or into oneself. It entered English through French in the seventeenth century, and psychology later gave it the technical sense of watching your own mind.
intro.cn: introspection 把拉丁语 intro（在内）与 specere（看）拼在一起，最初意为「看进去」，尤指看进事物或看进自身。它在十七世纪经由法语进入英语，后来心理学又赋予它「观察自己心智」的专门义。

items.en: Intro means within or inward, as in introire, to go inside.
items.cn: intro 意为在内、向内，如 introire 意为走进去。

items.en: Specere means to look; it lies behind spectare, to watch, and speculum, a mirror.
items.cn: specere 意为看，它也是 spectare（注视）与 speculum（镜子）的来源。

items.en: The compound introspectare appears in later Latin in the sense of looking into something.
items.cn: 较晚的拉丁语里出现 introspectare 这一组合，意为看进某物。

items.en: French introspection carries the inward look into early modern scholarly writing.
items.cn: 法语中的形制把「向内看」带进了近代早期的学术写作。

items.en: English adopts introspection first as a looking into things, later as a looking into oneself.
items.cn: 英语先借入「看进事物」的意思，后来才转向「看进自身」。

items.en: Psychology makes introspection the name of a method and a habit of mind.
items.cn: 心理学把 introspection 变成一种方法与心理习惯的名称。

note.en: The first group holds the intro- family built on the same looking root and its mirror image; the second group holds words for turning attention back on the self.
note.cn: 第一组是与 introspection 同根、同样建立在「看」上的词族及其镜像词；第二组是表示把注意力转回自身的近义词。

entries.definition: tending to look inward and examine your own thoughts
entries.definitionCN: 爱内省的；惯于审视自己念头的人

entries.definition: to examine your own thoughts and feelings
entries.definitionCN: 内省；反省（由名词逆构出的动词）

entries.definition: a look back at past events
entries.definitionCN: 回顾；回想（retro- 为「向后」，与 intro- 相反，但共用「看」词根）

entries.definition: the act of examining your own motives and actions
entries.definitionCN: 自我审视；自查

entries.definition: quiet serious thought about your own life and behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 反思；沉思

entries.definition: a clear knowledge of your own character and feelings
entries.definitionCN: 自我意识；自我觉察

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts, the intro- word family, and the phrases introspection actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词形、intro- 词族，以及 introspection 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Intro means within and specere means to look: introspection is a look within.
normal.cn: intro 意为在内，specere 意为看：introspection 就是往里面看。

normal.en: The family runs introspection, introspective, introspect, and introspectively.
normal.cn: 词族包括 introspection、introspective、introspect、introspectively。

normal.en: Honest introspection means looking at yourself without flattering the picture.
normal.cn: honest introspection 指不美化地看自己。

normal.en: Retrospect looks back at the past while introspection looks inward at the mind.
normal.cn: retrospect 向后看往事，introspection 向内看内心。

normal.en: Compare reflection: reflection is calmer and softer, introspection is more systematic and inward.
normal.cn: 对比 reflection：reflection 更平静温和，introspection 更条理、更向内。

abstract.en: See a person turning a headlamp away from the room and shining it into the chest.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把头灯从满屋转向自己的胸口，往里照。

abstract.en: Hear a scientist taking notes out loud about her own reactions.
abstract.cn: 想象一位科学家一边观察自己的反应，一边大声记下笔记。

abstract.en: See a long mirror propped beside a desk, catching every choice you make.
abstract.cn: 想象书桌旁支着一面长长的镜子，照出你每一个选择。

examples.en: Regular introspection helps him notice the fears that drive his choices.
examples.cn: 定期自省帮助他看清驱动自己选择的那些恐惧。

examples.en: The book rewards readers who bring patience and a taste for introspection.
examples.cn: 这本书回馈那些有耐心、喜欢审视内心的读者。

examples.en: Her first draft was pure introspection, all mood and no action.
examples.cn: 她的初稿全是内心独白，只有情绪没有情节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因戳视线」——像被一根针线戳着、把目光戳回自己身上，就是往内看；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intro（在内）+ specere（看）→ 拉丁语动词 introspectare（看进去）→ 法语 introspection → 英语 introspection，核心义「往里看，把目光转向自身」。同根词有 prospect（向前看）、retrospect（向后看）、spectacle（景象）。

sensesIntro.en: Introspection starts as the literal act of looking inward, then becomes a repeatable method, then a judgment of oneself, then a literary craft, and finally an older poetic power of seeing inside things.
sensesIntro.cn: introspection 先是字面上「往里看」的举动，再成为一种可重复的方法，又指对自身的评判，然后是文学中的写法，最后还保留着较古老的「看穿事物内部」这一诗语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who turns the inner gaze around and looks back at their own mind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人把内在的目光掉个头，回看自己的心智。

branches.en: The everyday sense is the simple habit of looking inward.
branches.cn: 日常义项就是「往心里看」这个简单习惯。

branches.en: Repetition and reporting turn the habit into a scientific method.
branches.cn: 反复进行并加以报告，使习惯变成一种科学方法。

branches.en: Judging what you see turns observation into self-examination.
branches.cn: 对所见的加以评判，观察就变成了反省。

branches.en: The same inward gaze becomes literature when it is written down for a reader.
branches.cn: 同一种向内看的目光一旦为读者写下，就成了文学。

branches.en: The older into sense stretches the looking beyond the self to the inside of things.
branches.cn: 较古老的「进入」义把目光从自身伸展到事物的内部。

intro.en: Introspection is built from the Latin prefix intro-, within, and the Latin root spec-, to look. The same look appears in prospect, retrospect, and inspect.
intro.cn: introspection 由拉丁语前缀 intro-（在内）与拉丁语词根 spec-（看）构成；同样的「看」也出现在 prospect、retrospect、inspect 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin intro means within and specere means to look; the noun combines them into an act of looking into something or into oneself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intro 意为在内，specere 意为看；这个名词把两者合成「看进某物或看进自身」的行为。

items.example: The prefix points the motion back toward the inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指回内部。

items.example: The root supplies the gaze at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供词核心处的目光。

items.example: Specere is the plain verb behind the root.
items.exampleCN: specere 是词根背后的原形动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -tion turns the action into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 把动作变成名词。

items.example: Introspection names the inward look itself.
items.exampleCN: introspection 指「往内看」这件事本身。

items.example: The suffix -ive makes the trait an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 把这特质变为形容词。

items.example: Introspect was cut back from the noun.
items.exampleCN: introspect 是把这个名词截短逆构出来的动词。

items.example: The adverb -ly marks the inward manner.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾 -ly 标出「向内」的方式。

items.example: Prospect adds pro-, forward, to the same look.
items.exampleCN: prospect 在同一「看」根前加了 pro-（向前）。

items.example: Retrospect turns the gaze backward instead.
items.exampleCN: retrospect 则把目光转向后方。

items.example: Inspect keeps the plain seeing sense.
items.exampleCN: inspect 保留了朴素的「看」义。

definition_zh: 内向的人；内倾者；内向性格者；性格中内向的一面
definition_en: a person who is quiet, turns attention inward, and regains energy in solitude rather than in groups
core_image: 一个人转过身面朝墙角，把热闹的房间留在背后
scene: 散场后，别人还在门口聊天，她一个人慢慢走回宿舍，只有独处时才觉得放松。At the party the introvert stayed near the bookshelf, answering questions with a smile and very few words.
sceneCN: 这里 introvert 是「内向的人」（第 1 个义项：安静、注意力朝内、靠独处恢复精力的人）；句意：聚会上，那个内向的人一直待在书架旁边，微笑着回答问题，却只说很少几个字。

pos.zh: 内向的人；内倾者；内向性格者；性格中内向的一面

collocations.zh: 内心深处那个内向的自己

derivatives.zh: introvert + -ed，义为「内向的；害羞的」
introvert + -sion，义为「内向性；内倾」

senses.title: A person who turns inward
senses.definition: a person who prefers quiet, thinks before speaking, and gains energy from being alone
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢安静、说话前先思考，并从独处中获得精力的人
senses.example: As a boy he was an introvert who read through every lunch break.
senses.exampleCN: 他小时候是个内向的孩子，每个午休都在看书。
senses.why: Latin intro means within and vertere means to turn, so an introvert is literally a person turned inward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 intro 意为「向内」，vertere 意为「转」：introvert 字面上就是「朝内转的人」。

senses.title: The psychological type
senses.definition: in psychology, a person whose attention and energy are directed inward rather than toward people and events outside
senses.definitionCN: 心理学上注意力与精力朝内、而非朝外部人与事的人
senses.example: For Jung the introvert draws strength from inner experience.
senses.exampleCN: 在荣格看来，内倾者从内心体验中获得力量。
senses.why: The word was coined as a technical label, so the inward turn became a named, describable personality type.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是作为术语造出来的，于是「朝内转」变成了一种有名有姓、可以描述的人格类型。

senses.title: The inward side of a personality
senses.definition: the quiet, inward part of a personality, even in someone who is generally outgoing
senses.definitionCN: 性格中安静、朝内的一面，即使这个人整体上是外向的
senses.example: Loud on stage, she is an introvert once the microphone is off.
senses.exampleCN: 她在台上很放得开，一放下麦克风却是个内向的人。
senses.why: The same inward turn can be imagined as one side of a person, so even a lively person can name the introvert inside.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「朝内转」可以被想象成性格中的一面，因此即便是外向的人也能指认自己心里那个内向的自己。

senses.title: The animal that turns in
senses.definition: an animal, usually a worm, whose certain body parts can be drawn back inside itself
senses.definitionCN: 某些身体部位能缩回体内的动物，多为蠕虫
senses.example: Biologists classed the worm as an introvert.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家把这种蠕虫归为可缩回体内的那一类。
senses.why: The same turning word was borrowed by zoology, where the inward movement is a body part pulled back inside the tube of an organism.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「转」的词被动物学借用，那里朝内的动作指的是身体的一部分缩回生物体的管腔里。

intro.en: Introvert is a Latin-style compound of intro, within, and vertere, to turn, so its root meaning is a turning inward. Early modern writers used it of plants and parts that fold inward before it took on the psychological sense around the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: introvert 是仿拉丁语构成的复合词：intro（向内）加 vertere（转），词根义就是「向内转」。近代早期作家先用它指向里卷的植物和器官，大约在二十世纪初才获得心理学含义。

items.en: Intro means within or inward, the direction of the motion.
items.cn: intro 意为向内，表示动作的方向。

items.en: Vertere means to turn; once more it supplies the turning element.
items.cn: vertere 意为转，在这里再次提供「转」的成分。

items.en: Introvert is first used in natural history for parts that turn or fold inward, and in Latin-style school exercises.
items.cn: introvert 最初用于博物学，指向内转或内折的部分；也见诸仿拉丁语的学校练习。

items.en: The psychologist Carl Jung speaks of the introvertierte personality, whose interest turns inward.
items.cn: 心理学家荣格谈到 introvertierte 人格，即兴趣朝内转的类型。

items.en: English takes introvert up as the name of a psychological type, set against extrovert.
items.cn: 英语把这个词借来作心理学类型的名称，与 extrovert 相对。

items.en: The clinical label widens into everyday use for any quiet, inward-looking person or trait.
items.cn: 这个临床标签扩大为日常用语，指任何安静、向内看的人或特质。

note.en: The first group holds the introvert word family and its outward-facing opposite; the second group holds everyday words for quiet, inward-looking people.
note.cn: 第一组是 introvert 的同族词与朝外的相反构词；第二组是日常用来形容安静、向内看的人的说法。

entries.definition: a person who is outgoing and gains energy from others
entries.definitionCN: 外向的人（由 extra-「向外」加 vertere 构成，与本词方向相反）

entries.definition: quiet and inward-looking
entries.definitionCN: 内向的；不爱交际的

entries.definition: the quality of being inward-looking
entries.definitionCN: 内向性；内倾

entries.definition: nervous with people you do not know
entries.definitionCN: 害羞的；怕生的

entries.definition: keeping your feelings and opinions to yourself
entries.definitionCN: 矜持的；不爱表露的

entries.definition: a person who likes to be alone
entries.definitionCN: 孤僻的人；独来独往的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts, the introvert word family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词形、introvert 同族词，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Intro means within and vertere means to turn: an introvert is a person turned inward.
normal.cn: intro 意为向内，vertere 意为转：introvert 就是朝内转的人。

normal.en: The family runs introvert, introverted, introversion, with extrovert as the mirror image.
normal.cn: 词族包括 introvert、introverted、introversion，而 extrovert 是它的镜像反义。

normal.en: A natural introvert is someone for whom a quiet room is the default setting.
normal.cn: a natural introvert 指默认状态就待在安静房间里的人。

normal.en: To come across as an introvert means you seem quiet even when you are not.
normal.cn: come across as an introvert 意为给人安静的印象，即使你并非如此。

normal.en: Compare reserved: reserved focuses on holding feelings back, introvert focuses on the inward direction of energy.
normal.cn: 对比 reserved：reserved 强调把情绪收起来，introvert 强调精力朝内。

abstract.en: Picture a person facing a wall while the party noise stays behind them.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人面朝墙壁，聚会的喧闹声留在背后。

abstract.en: See a phone whose charger is plugged into the user instead of the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一部手机把充电线插进使用者身上，而不是墙上的插座。

abstract.en: Imagine a snail drawing itself in and closing the shell on the crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蜗牛把自己缩进去，把壳对着人群合上。

examples.en: The teacher learned to give introverts time to think before pressing them for answers.
examples.cn: 老师学会了在追问答案之前，先给内向的学生一些思考的时间。

examples.en: As an introvert she finds networking events far more tiring than the work itself.
examples.cn: 作为一个内向的人，她觉得社交活动远比工作本身更让人疲惫。

examples.en: Open-plan offices are often harder on introverts than on their louder colleagues.
examples.cn: 开放式办公室对内向者的困扰，往往比对爱说话的同事更大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引戳我」——像被戳了一下，赶紧把心往里收回来，就是内向的人；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 intro（在内）+ vertere（转）→ 仿拉丁语复合词 introvert（朝内转的人）→ 英语 introvert；核心义「心思朝内转的人」。同根词有 convert（转变）、divert（使转向）、reverse（反转）。

sensesIntro.en: Introvert begins as the person turned inward, becomes a psychological type set against extrovert, then names the quiet side of any personality, and finally passes into zoology for a body part folded back inside.
sensesIntro.cn: introvert 起初指「朝内转的人」，随后成为与 extrovert 相对的心理学类型，又指任何人性格中安静内向的一面，最后进入动物学，指缩回体内的器官。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose face and attention are turned inward, away from the busy room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人把脸和注意力都朝内转，背对着喧闹的房间。

branches.en: The everyday sense is simply the quiet person who turns inward.
branches.cn: 日常义项就是那个安静、朝内转的人。

branches.en: Psychology turns that posture into a named type set against the extrovert.
branches.cn: 心理学把这种姿态变成与 extrovert 相对的有名类型。

branches.en: The inward turn can also be one side of a loud personality.
branches.cn: 朝内转也可以是一个开朗人士性格中的一面。

branches.en: Both uses share the same inward direction, spoken of as a whole person or as a single side.
branches.cn: 两种用法共享同一个朝内的方向，只是有时指整个人、有时指某一面。

branches.en: Zoology reuses the literal turning movement for a body part drawn back inside.
branches.cn: 动物学把字面的「转」用于缩回体内的器官。

intro.en: Introvert puts the Latin prefix intro-, within, in front of the Latin verb vertere, to turn. The same turning appears in extrovert, convert, divert, and reverse.
intro.cn: introvert 把拉丁语前缀 intro-（向内）放在拉丁语动词 vertere（转）前面；同样的「转」也出现在 extrovert、convert、divert、reverse 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin intro means within and vertere means to turn; the same two parts build introvert and its opposite extrovert.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 intro 意为向内，vertere 意为转；同样的两部分构成了 introvert 及其相反的 extrovert。

items.example: The prefix points the motion back toward the self.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指回自身。

items.example: Vertere is the turning verb at the heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: vertere 是这个词核心处的「转」动词。

items.example: Convert and divert both end in the same turning element.
items.exampleCN: convert 与 divert 都以同一个表示「转」的成分结尾。

items.example: Introvert names the person who faces inward.
items.exampleCN: introvert 指朝内转的那类人。

items.example: The suffix -ed makes the turned-inward manner an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 把朝内的举止变成形容词。

items.example: The suffix -sion makes it the name of the trait.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -sion 使它成为这一特质的名称。

items.example: Extrovert swaps the prefix to extra-, outside.
items.exampleCN: extrovert 把前缀换成了 extra-（在外）。

items.example: Convert adds con-, together, to the turning root.
items.exampleCN: convert 在「转」词根前加了 con-（一起）。

items.example: Divert turns something away from its path.
items.exampleCN: divert 把某物从原路上转开。

items.example: Reverse adds re-, back, to the same root.
items.exampleCN: reverse 在同一词根前加了 re-（向后）。

definition_zh: 侵入；闯入；打扰；侵扰；强加；伸入（地质）
definition_en: to enter a place, situation, or conversation where you are not wanted or not expected
core_image: 一扇没被邀请的门被推开，陌生人把半个身子探了进来
scene: 一家人正在吃晚饭，门没有敲，一个陌生人已经站在了客厅中央。She did not want to intrude on their private celebration, so she left the gift on the step.
sceneCN: 这里 intrude 是「闯入、打扰」（第 1 个义项：进入不属于自己的场合且不受欢迎）；句意：她不想打扰他们私下的庆祝，就把礼物放在了台阶上。

collocations.zh: 侵扰；打扰（某人隐私或时刻）
打扰；打扰（正式说法，多指打断安宁）
（念头等）强行闯入（某人的意识）

derivatives.zh: intrude + -sion，义为「侵入；闯入；侵扰」
intrude + -er，义为「入侵者；闯入者」
intrude + -ive，义为「侵扰的；打扰人的；侵入性的」
intrusive + -ly，义为「以侵扰的方式」
non- + intrusive，义为「非侵入式的；不打扰的」

senses.title: To enter where you are not wanted
senses.definition: to enter a place or situation where you are not invited and not wanted
senses.definitionCN: 进入并未被邀请、也不受欢迎的地方或场合
senses.example: Reporters kept intruding into the garden where the children were playing.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们一再到孩子们玩耍的花园里闯进来。
senses.why: Latin in means into and trudere means to thrust, so the word pictures a body pushed into a space it was kept out of.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in 意为「进入」，trudere 意为「推」：这个词的画面就是身体被推进一个本被挡在外面的空间。

senses.title: To disturb a private moment
senses.definition: to interrupt or disturb someone who is resting, grieving, or concentrating
senses.definitionCN: 打断或打扰正在休息、悲伤或专注的人
senses.example: I did not want to intrude while she was resting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在休息时，我不想打扰她。
senses.why: Once the private room is the space, the inward push becomes an interruption of someone private state rather than of a room.
senses.whyCN: 当被推进的「空间」从房间变成一个人的状态，这种向内的推挤就变成了对某种私人时刻的打断。

senses.title: To press something unwanted on others
senses.definition: to force your views, worries, or feelings on other people who did not ask for them
senses.definitionCN: 把看法、忧虑或情绪强加给并未索取的人
senses.example: He intruded his opinions into every family dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他每次家庭聚餐都要把自己的意见塞进去。
senses.why: The same thrust breaks into someone else territory, so thoughts and advice can be pushed on a person as well as a body into a room.
senses.whyCN: 同样的推挤闯进了别人的地盘，所以被推进去的既可以是身体闯进房间，也可以是想法和建议硬塞给别人。

senses.title: Of physical forces
senses.definition: of water, salt, or cold air, to spread into a place it does not normally reach
senses.definitionCN: 水、盐分或冷空气扩散进平时到不了的地方
senses.example: Seawater can intrude into the freshwater aquifer.
senses.exampleCN: 海水可能侵入淡水含水层。
senses.why: Not all intruders are people; anything that moves where it is not expected, from salt water to a cold draught, uses the same pushing image.
senses.whyCN: 闯进来的不一定是人：从咸水到冷风，任何进入「本不该出现之处」的东西都沿用同一个推挤的画面。

senses.title: Of magma and old rock
senses.definition: in geology, of molten rock, to force its way into older surrounding rock
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学中，指熔融岩浆挤入更古老的围岩
senses.example: Granite intruded the layers as thick dykes.
senses.exampleCN: 花岗岩作为厚大的岩墙侵入了这些岩层。
senses.why: In geology the thrust is the magma that pushes into the older rock, and the general word becomes a precise technical term.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学中，推挤者就是挤进古老岩层的岩浆，这个普通词于是成了精确的术语。

intro.en: Intrude comes from Latin intrudere, from in, into, and trudere, to thrust or push away, so it pictures a thing pushed in where it was not invited. It enters English in the sixteenth century through French intruder.
intro.cn: intrude 来自拉丁语 intrudere，由 in（进入）与 trudere（推、挤）构成，画面就是「被硬推进本没被请进的地方」。它在十六世纪经由法语 intruder 进入英语。

items.en: Trudere means to thrust or push, and it also gives English extrude and intrude.
items.cn: trudere 意为推、挤，英语的 extrude 与 intrude 都由它而来。

items.en: In means into, so intrudere means to thrust something into a place.
items.cn: in 意为进入，所以 intrudere 意为把某物推挤进某处。

items.en: French intruder carries the sense of forcing oneself in.
items.cn: 法语 intruder 带上了「强行挤进去」的意思。

items.en: English uses intrude for people who force their way into places or affairs.
items.cn: 英语用 intrude 指硬闯进某地或干涉他人事务的人。

items.en: Science borrows the word: salt water intrudes, and molten rock intrudes older layers.
items.cn: 科学借用了这个词：咸水会侵入，熔岩会侵入更古老的岩层。

items.en: The everyday sense of disturbing a private moment keeps the same unwelcome push.
items.cn: 现代英语中「打扰私人时刻」的日常义，仍保留着同一种不受欢迎的推挤。

note.en: The first group holds the intrude word family and its opposite thrusting prefix; the second group holds words for breaking in uninvited.
note.cn: 第一组是 intrude 的同族词与相反方向的前缀构词；第二组是表示「不请自来地进入」的近义词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts, the intrude word family, and the preposition patterns the verb actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁词形、intrude 同族词，以及这个动词实际搭配的介词结构。

normal.en: In means into and trudere means to push: intrude is to push your way in.
normal.cn: in 意为进入，trudere 意为推：intrude 就是把自己硬推进去。

normal.en: The family runs intrude, intrusion, intruder, intrusive, and the opposite extrude.
normal.cn: 词族包括 intrude、intrusion、intruder、intrusive，以及方向相反的 extrude。

normal.en: With on or upon the word warns of privacy; with into it points at space.
normal.cn: 与 on 或 upon 搭配时意在提醒隐私，与 into 搭配时指空间。

normal.en: Unwilling to intrude is the polite formula for declining an invitation.
normal.cn: unwilling to intrude 是婉拒邀请的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Compare interrupt: interrupt stops a flow, intrude breaks into a private or guarded space.
normal.cn: 对比 interrupt：interrupt 打断的是流程，intrude 闯入的是私人或有界限的空间。

abstract.en: Hear a door opening with no knock first.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门没等人敲就先开了。

abstract.en: See a hand parting the curtain of a lit living room.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手拨开亮着灯的客厅窗帘。

abstract.en: Feel a worry pushing in just as you fall asleep.
abstract.cn: 感受一阵担忧在你正要睡着时硬挤进来。

examples.en: The rules stop journalists from intruding on the family during the trial.
examples.cn: 这些规定禁止记者在庭审期间打扰这个家庭。

examples.en: Salt water intruded into the aquifer after the wells were drilled.
examples.cn: 水井开凿之后，海水侵入了含水层。

examples.en: As the meeting grew late, she felt it was time to stop intruding.
examples.cn: 会议开得很晚，她觉得该停止打扰了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因闯入」——听成「硬闯的」，不敲门就挤进来；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in（进入）+ trudere（推、挤）→ 拉丁语 intrudere（硬推进去）→ 法语 intruder → 英语 intrude；核心义「把自己或某物硬推进不该进的地方」。反向前缀同根词 extrude 意为挤出；同族词有 intrusion、intruder、intrusive、unobtrusive。

sensesIntro.en: Intrude starts with a body pushing into a place it was shut out of, moves to the same push against a private moment, then it presses thoughts on other people, and finally passes into science for water and molten rock.
sensesIntro.cn: intrude 先指身体硬挤进一个本被挡在外面的地方，进而指对私人时刻的推挤、对别人观点的强加，最后进入科学语域，指海水与熔岩的侵入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that is pushed through a doorway that was not opened for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体被推到一扇并未为它打开的门里。

branches.en: The literal sense is a person pushing into a place, its territory, or a private space.
branches.cn: 字面义是人硬闯进某处、某人的地盘或私人空间。

branches.en: The same push against a sheltered moment becomes an interruption.
branches.cn: 同样的推挤撞向受保护的私人时刻，就成了打断。

branches.en: Pushing opinions into a conversation carries the force to ideas.
branches.cn: 把意见硬推进对话，就是把这种推力用在想法上。

branches.en: A body and a tide both break a boundary, one on foot and one by flow.
branches.cn: 身体与潮流都在越过界限，一个靠双脚，一个靠流动。

branches.en: Geology names the same thrust when magma forces its way into old rock.
branches.cn: 地质学把岩浆挤进古老岩层的同一种推挤命名为侵入。

intro.en: Intrude is built from the Latin prefix in-, into, and the Latin verb trudere, to push. The reverse, a pushing out, is extrude.
intro.cn: intrude 由拉丁语前缀 in-（进入）与拉丁语动词 trudere（推）构成；反过来「往外推」就是 extrude。

latinIntro.en: Latin in means into and trudere means to push or thrust; together they mean to push something in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in 意为进入，trudere 意为推、挤；两者合起来就是「把东西推挤进去」。

items.example: The prefix directs the thrust inward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把推力指向内部。

items.example: Trudere supplies the pushing movement.
items.exampleCN: trudere 提供推挤的动作。

items.example: Intrude and extrude share the pushing element.
items.exampleCN: intrude 与 extrude 共享「推」的成分。

items.example: Intrude keeps the full pushing image.
items.exampleCN: intrude 完整保留了推挤的画面。

items.example: The suffix -sion forms intrusion.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -sion 构成 intrusion。

items.example: Intrusion names the act itself.
items.exampleCN: intrusion 指这行为本身。

items.example: The suffix -er marks the person who pushes in.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 标出那个推挤进来的人。

items.example: The suffix -ive turns the act into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 把行为变成一种性质。

items.example: The adverb -ly marks the unwelcome manner.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾 -ly 标出那种不受欢迎的方式。

items.example: The prefix non- denies the invasion.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 non- 否定这种侵入。

items.example: Extrude swaps in for the reverse direction ex-, out.
items.exampleCN: extrude 把 in- 换成反方向的 ex-（向外）。
